name: Astryx (@astryxdesign/core)
oneLiner: Meta's open-source React 19 design system, authored in StyleX but shipped as prebuilt layered CSS. It has 150+ accessible components, CSS-variable themes (7 published), page templates, and a CLI aimed at AI agents (docs, swizzle/eject, theme build, codemods).

stack.framework: React 19+ only (peer react/react-dom >=19.0.0). Uses React 19 features: ref as a prop, with forwardRef banned by lint; use(); useTransition for async actions; useOptimistic for inputs. The docs cover Next.js App Router, Vite and a no-build CDN setup (esm.sh import map). Components are 'use client'.
stack.styling: Authored in StyleX (peer @stylexjs/stylex ^0.19.0). Consumers import prebuilt CSS in cascade layers: reset.css (@layer reset), astryx.css (@layer astryx-base), theme.css (@layer astryx-theme). Tokens are CSS custom properties such as --color-accent, --color-on-accent, --color-background-surface, --radius-element and --spacing-1..10. Dark mode uses light-dark() with [light, dark] tuples. Escape hatches, in priority order: xstyle, then className, then style. A Tailwind v4 bridge (@astryxdesign/core/tailwind-theme.css, using @theme reference inline) maps tokens to bg-surface, text-primary, rounded-lg and similar utilities.
stack.headlessPrimitives: None. No Radix, React Aria or Floating UI. The only runtime dependency is intl-messageformat. Overlays are built on the native Popover API, <dialog> and CSS anchor positioning (position-area, position-try-fallbacks), with in-house hooks such as useLayer, useFocusTrap and useListFocus.
stack.animation: In-house. CSS transitions and keyframes driven by duration tokens: --duration-fast 175ms, --duration-medium 410ms, --duration-slow 975ms, each with -min and -max. Easing tokens are --ease-standard, --ease-entrance, --ease-move and --ease-exit. A JS animator (createAnimator, createPanGesture) plus a table of UIKit/SwiftUI springs measured on iOS (packages/core/src/motion/uikit/springs.ts) drives touch gestures: segmented lens, sheets, toast swipe. Themes set tempo (0.75–1.5) and character (crisp, standard or expressive). Under reduced motion, changes are instant with a fine pointer and a cross-fade of 200ms or less with a coarse pointer. Not built on the motion package.
stack.other: i18n uses intl-messageformat plus Crowdin. 30 locale bundles in packages/core/locales include ar-SA, he-IL and tr-TR, but there is no id, th or sw bundle. RTL is detected through Intl.Locale textInfo (getLocaleDirection), and all props use logical start/end naming. Calendar supports non-Gregorian systems through Intl. Docs are structured *.doc.mjs metadata per component (props, do/don't, WCAG criteria, anatomy, theming targets, a zh translation and a terse 'dense' AI version) that feed the docs site, Storybook and the CLI. Tests use Vitest and Playwright, including a11y, interaction and perf configs. The npm package is about 28 MB unpacked across 4,610 files, with per-component subpath exports.

distribution: npm: @astryxdesign/core (components, theme system, hooks) plus @astryxdesign/theme-{neutral,butter,chocolate,matcha,stone,gothic,y2k}. @astryxdesign/cli is a dev dependency: component and hook docs, search, template scaffolding (57 page templates in the sitemap: dashboard, settings, table-page, login, kanban-board and others), theme add/build, swizzle to eject a component's source into your project, upgrade --apply codemods (also refreshes ShadCN-copied components), and init, which writes a component index into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. Also @astryxdesign/build (StyleX source-build plugins) and @astryxdesign/richtext. @astryxdesign/charts and vega are published under the canary tag only. A CDN ESM path works through an esm.sh import map, and a Figma community file exists. Latest is 0.7.9, published 2026-11-06. The README says 'Currently in Beta'.

standout.name: Button
standout.why: The most carefully engineered button found in this research, and directly relevant to a sizes and variants Button plus a possible ButtonV2. Source read: packages/core/src/Button/Button.tsx (1,024 lines). It handles async actions, link rendering, tooltip naming, group corners, RTL and touch press.
standout.apiNotes: `label: string` is required and becomes the accessible name. Optional children override only the visible text, with label kept as aria-label. variant: 'primary'|'secondary'|'ghost'|'destructive' (default 'secondary'). size: 'sm'|'md'|'lg' = 28/32/36px, inherited from SizeContext through useSize(prop,'md'). elevation: 'none'|'low'|'med'|'high' for FABs. isDisabled. isLoading. clickAction(e) => void|Promise runs in useTransition: it shows a spinner, sets aria-busy, blocks re-clicks and announces 'Loading' in a live region. The spinner and content swap are delayed by --duration-medium-min so fast actions never flash. isInterruptible lets a re-click restart the action. icon (leading) and endContent (trailing badge or chevron) use logical start/end naming. isIconOnly. width (number = px, string as-is). tooltip uses aria-disabled instead of native disabled so a disabled button stays focusable. href/as/target/rel render an <a> or a custom Link, through LinkProvider or a per-button `as`; a disabled link-button falls back to <button>. Variants are typed from `interface ButtonVariantMap`, which themes extend through TypeScript module augmentation. themeProps('button',{variant,size,elevation}) emits class 'astryx-button' plus data-variant/data-size/data-elevation. Themeable vars: --button-focus-offset, --button-icon-only-aspect. There is no outline variant and no asChild: polymorphism is limited to link rendering via `as`.

standout.name: ButtonGroup / IconButton / ToggleButton(Group)
standout.why: A clean split into separate components instead of one overloaded Button. The group supplies size and disabled state through context and handles joined corners correctly even when tooltips or popovers are siblings.
standout.apiNotes: ButtonGroup: children, label (required, used as aria-label), orientation 'horizontal'|'vertical', size (a default that children may override), isDisabled, elevation shared by the whole group. IconButton: label (required), icon (required), the same variant/size/elevation/isLoading/clickAction/isInterruptible/tooltip/href/as props as Button. ToggleButton: isPressed, onPressedChange(isPressed, event) (preventDefault vetoes the change), pressedChangeAction for async toggles, pressedIcon, and value when used inside ToggleButtonGroup.

standout.name: NumberInput
standout.why: A counter or stepper input whose behaviour has been thought through, which fits the 'sayaç arttırma' (counter/stepper) need.
standout.apiNotes: label (required), value: number|null (required), onChange(value) (required) fires on blur, Enter, a stepper click or clear, not on every keystroke. min and max clamp on commit. step = 1. formatValue(value) shows formatted text when blurred and the raw number on focus. hasNumberSteppers shows ± buttons on fine pointers only and hides them on touch. isWheelEnabled = true. units ('%', 'GB'). isIntegerOnly. hasClear, which also allows onChange(null). isReadOnly versus isDisabled plus disabledMessage. status {type:'error'|'warning'|'success', message?} with statusVariant 'attached'|'detached'|'tooltip'. Shared field props: description, isOptional/isRequired, labelTooltip, startIcon, labelIcon. A three-way styling split: container*/control* × Xstyle/ClassName/Style.

standout.name: Calendar / DateRangeInput
standout.why: Strong i18n for a calendar: non-Gregorian systems, ISO date strings and range constraints. That matters for an 18-locale site that includes ar.
standout.apiNotes: Calendar: mode 'single'|'range'. value (ISODateString | DateRange | null) or defaultValue, with onChange. numberOfMonths 1|2. min/max are ISODateString, a template-literal type for 'YYYY-MM-DD'. dateConstraints: Array<(date)=>boolean>. maxRangeSpan/minRangeSpan count both endpoints. focusDate/onFocusDateChange give a controlled visible month. handleRef exposes navigateTo(). hasOutsideDays, hasWeekNumbers (ISO), hasVariableRowCount, weekStartsOn (0–6 or 'mon' etc.). calendar: 'gregory'|'persian'|'hebrew'|'islamic-umalqura'|'japanese'|…, defaulting to the InternationalizationProvider setting. DateRangeInput adds presets (quick ranges beside the calendar), hasClear, changeAction (async, useTransition), and numberOfMonths defaulting to 2.

standout.name: Card / ClickableCard / SelectableCard
standout.why: Three cards with distinct semantics instead of one card with an onClick prop. Each gets the correct role, focus and link behaviour.
standout.apiNotes: Card: padding uses spacing steps 0|0.5|1|1.5|2|3|4|5|6|8|10, and omitting it takes the theme's card padding. variant: 'default'|'transparent'|'muted'|hue names (blue, cyan, gray, green, orange, pink, purple, red, teal, yellow). elevation none|low|med|high. width/height/maxWidth/minHeight accept SizeValue. ClickableCard: label (required), onClick or href/target with Cmd- and middle-click handled, isDisabled keeps the tab stop. SelectableCard: label, isSelected and onChange(isSelected) (all required); the selection ring composes on top of the elevation shadow.

standout.name: Table + plugin hooks
standout.why: The best fit for admin panels. It is data-driven, and behaviours are composable headless plugins rather than dozens of boolean props.
standout.apiNotes: <Table data columns idKey density='compact'|'balanced'|'spacious' dividers='rows'|'columns'|'grid'|'none' isStriped hasHover verticalAlign textOverflow='wrap'|'truncate' rowIndexStart rowCount plugins={{sort, selection, …}} />. Columns take {key, header, width: proportional(n,{minWidth})|pixel(n), align, renderCell}. Plugins are hooks: useTableSortable({sort, onSortChange, allowUnsortedState, isMultiSortEnabled}) with direction 'ascending'|'descending', plus useTableSelection, useTablePagination, useTableFiltering, useTableColumnResize, useTableStickyColumns, useTableRowExpansion, useTableTreeData, useTableGroupedRows and useTableColumnSettings. Children mode composes TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow and TableCell by hand. TableSelectionToolbar handles bulk actions.

standout.name: AppShell
standout.why: A slot-based admin or user-panel frame that handles independent scroll areas and the mobile drawer.
standout.apiNotes: Slots: topNav, sideNav, banner, children (rendered in <main>). contentPadding takes a spacing step and is documented as 4 for forms and 0 for tables or dashboards. height: 'fill' (100dvh, independent scroll containers) or 'auto'. variant: 'wash'|'surface'|'section'|'elevated' controls nav-versus-content contrast. useAppShellMobile handles the drawer. Pairs with SideNav and TopNav sub-part families and the Layout header, content and panel slots used by templates.

standout.name: CommandPalette
standout.why: A Cmd-K palette with a pluggable search-source abstraction, useful for admin panels.
standout.apiNotes: isOpen and onOpenChange (required). searchSource: SearchSource<T> exposes search(query) and bootstrap(), with createStaticSource for static lists. input and footer slots default to CommandPaletteInput and CommandPaletteFooter. renderItem(item, isSelected) is for presentation only. emptySearchText and emptyBootstrapText. A picker mode uses value and onValueChange. width = 640, maxHeight = 480. isInline renders without a modal. Sub-parts: Group, Item, List, Empty, Footer.

standout.name: Toast / useToast
standout.why: An imperative toast API with deduplication, sensible persistence rules and swipe-to-dismiss.
standout.apiNotes: const showToast = useToast(); const dismiss = showToast({body, type: 'info'|'error', isAutoHide, autoHideDuration = 5000, endContent (Undo button), uniqueID, collisionBehavior: 'overwrite'|'ignore', onHide(reason)}). Error toasts persist until dismissed by default. renderContent replaces the card's content while keeping the theme target and auto-hide. Works with LayerProvider or mounts its own viewport. Swipe dismissal lives in useToastGesture.ts.

standout.name: SegmentedControl
standout.why: Shows how to make a small control feel native. The selection 'lens' slides with springs measured on iOS and follows touch.
standout.apiNotes: value, onChange and label are required (label is used only as aria-label). size sm|md|lg. layout 'hug'|'fill'. isDisabled plus disabledMessage. Children are SegmentedControlItem. Motion lives in useSegmentedSelectionMotion.ts (53 KB) and useSegmentedTouchTracking.ts. The theme overrides item height through components['segmented-control-item']['size:sm'].

standout.name: ProgressBar / EmptyState / Timer
standout.why: Small dashboard pieces with precise APIs.
standout.apiNotes: ProgressBar: label (required), value/max, hasValueLabel, formatValueLabel(value,max), variant accent|success|warning|error|neutral, isIndeterminate (pulses under reduced motion), marks: [{value,label}] for goal lines, isDisabled. EmptyState: title (required), description, icon (decorative), actions, headingLevel 1–6 (semantics only), isCompact. Timer: startTime (epoch ms), format 'elapsed'|'clock', plus Text props (type, size, color, weight).

standout.name: Stack (HStack / VStack)
standout.why: The layout primitive behind every template. It uses numeric spacing steps and logical, RTL-safe padding.
standout.apiNotes: direction. gap and padding take numbers 0|0.5|1|1.5|2|3|4|5|6|8|10, not strings. paddingInline/Block/InlineStart/InlineEnd/BlockStart/BlockEnd. hAlign/vAlign are axis-independent alignment, with justify/align aliases. 'between' is used, not 'space-between'. wrap, isScrollable, width/height/maxWidth/minHeight, as.

buttonApi:
Button props (from packages/core/src/Button/Button.tsx and Button.doc.mjs):
- Content: `label: string` is required. It is the visible text and the accessible name. Optional `children` overrides the visible text only.
- variant: 'primary' | 'secondary' (default) | 'ghost' | 'destructive'. There is no outline variant.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' (default) | 'lg', which map to --size-element-*. The API conventions put these at 28/32/36px. Size is inherited from SizeContext through ButtonGroup or InputGroup.
- elevation: 'none' | 'low' | 'med' | 'high', for FABs. It is ignored inside a group.
- Loading: isLoading; clickAction (async, useTransition-based, with a delayed spinner, aria-busy, re-click dedupe and a live-region announcement); isInterruptible.
- Icons: icon (leading) and endContent (trailing, inherits the variant colour); isIconOnly gives a square button with label as aria-label. A separate IconButton component also exists.
- Other: width (SizeValue) and tooltip.
- Link rendering: href, as (a custom link component), target and rel. LinkProvider sets the default link component app-wide, for example Next or next-intl Link.
- Escape hatches: xstyle, className, style.
- Not supported: asChild, render props, an outline variant, or colour as a separate prop.
- Groups: ButtonGroup (label, orientation, size, isDisabled, elevation) gives joined borders and radii. ToggleButton and ToggleButtonGroup use isPressed, onPressedChange and pressedChangeAction.
- Theming:
  - Stable class `astryx-button` plus data-variant, data-size and data-elevation.
  - Theme overrides via defineTheme({components: {button: {'variant:destructive': {...}}}}). An unknown `prop:value` key creates a new variant, and `theme build` emits the TypeScript augmentation of ButtonVariantMap.
apiPatterns:
Strict, written prop grammar (wiki: API-Conventions):
- booleans use is* for state and has* for features
- uncontrolled props are default* (defaultIsOpen)
- callbacks are on{Verb}{Scope?}
- async twins drop 'on' (clickAction, changeAction)
- primary change callback is onChange, not onValueChange
- direction is start/end, never left/right
- 'html' prefix only for true native passthroughs (htmlName)
Behavioral and structural props are required (label on every interactive control, value/onChange on controlled ones); presentation props are optional with defaults.
Async-first React 19 actions: clickAction runs in useTransition and changeAction uses useOptimistic. The busy state never drops focus: aria-busy plus aria-disabled plus guards, not native disabled.

themeProps(component, visualProps) gives each component one stable kebab-case class (astryx-progress-bar-fill; never run-together names) and reflects visual props and states as data-* attributes. This is a public theming surface that does not depend on generated class names.
Extensible variant unions via TypeScript module augmentation of exported *VariantMap interfaces, paired with theme component overrides keyed 'variant:x', 'size:sm', base or a state name.

Themes are plain CSS custom-property overrides with [light, dark] tuple values compiled to light-dark(). Also: scale generators (typography base/ratio, radius, motion tempo/character), conditional 'adaptations' (pointer, width, contrast, motion), and 'extends' inheritance. Built themes are SSR-safe CSS; runtime themes are for editors and prototypes.
Cascade-layer contract (reset, astryx-base, astryx-theme, then utilities) so a consumer's Tailwind className always wins over component defaults.
Styling escape hatches in fixed priority (xstyle, then className, then style), merged with mergeProps(). Compound inputs split container* and control* styling props.
SizeContext: groups set a size that descendants inherit unless they set their own (useSize(prop, default)).
LinkProvider plus a per-component `as`: one app-level injection of the router Link for every href-capable component.

Slots are passthrough (slotName={<X/>}, not wrapped or hoisted). Behaviours are hooks or boolean-or-config props, not wrapper components. Composition components (AppShell, Table) take slots, children and render functions; utilities take config props.
Headless plugin pipeline for Table (plugins={{sort: useTableSortable(...)}}) instead of boolean feature flags.
disabledMessage: a disabled control stays focusable via aria-disabled and explains why in a tooltip, instead of wrapping disabled controls in Tooltip.
Accessibility is specified per component in docs: the WCAG criterion, the required ratio and which states to test (rest, hover, pressed, focus), plus anatomy and do/don't lists.
RTL and i18n built in: logical properties everywhere, getLocaleDirection via Intl.Locale textInfo, component strings through a translator with an English fallback, Intl calendars.

Reduced motion distinguishes pointer type: instant with a fine pointer, an opacity cross-fade of 200ms or less with a coarse pointer. Press-scale is skipped under reduced motion and on touch, where :active is unreliable.
No headless dependency: overlays use the native Popover API plus CSS anchor positioning, and focus and dismissal are handled by in-house hooks.

Docs as data: each component ships Name.doc.mjs (props, bestPractices, accessibility, anatomy, theming targets, translations, a terse 'dense' AI variant) that drives the docs site, Storybook, CLI and AGENTS.md. The repo also has a CLAUDE.md, an AGENTS.md and 'vibe tests' for AI authoring.
swizzle: eject a component's full source into your project when the public API is not enough.
borrow: Adopt the prop grammar wholesale for your own library: is*/has*, default*, on{Verb}, async *Action twins, start/end, label required on interactive components, onChange as the primary callback. It is internally consistent and easy for AI agents to predict.

Button: copy the behaviour model rather than the StyleX code. Specifically: clickAction plus useTransition, a spinner delayed about 300ms so fast actions do not flash, aria-busy plus aria-disabled (focus kept), a live-region 'Loading', re-click dedupe, an isInterruptible escape, label as the accessible name with optional visible children, and link rendering only when not disabled. Add your own 'outline' (and 'tonal' if you mirror M3 filled/tonal/outlined/text) via the VariantMap pattern rather than a separate ButtonV2.

Reflect variants and states as data-* attributes plus one stable class per component part. In Tailwind v4 this lets themes and consumers target data-[variant=primary]: or [data-size=sm] without forking. It combines well with cva.
Make variant unions extensible with `export interface ButtonVariantMap {…}` plus module augmentation, so a project can add a variant without editing the library.

LinkProvider: one provider at the root injects `Link` from '@/i18n/navigation' into every href-capable component (Button, IconButton, ClickableCard, nav items). This enforces your next-intl locale-prefix rule at the library level.
SizeContext and useSize(prop, default) so ButtonGroup, InputGroup and toolbars size their children.

A standard Field contract for every input: label, isLabelHidden, description, isOptional/isRequired, status {type, message}, statusVariant, labelTooltip, startIcon, disabledMessage, and container/control className splits.
NumberInput semantics for your counter: commit on blur or Enter, clamp to min/max, formatValue when blurred and the raw number when focused, steppers hidden on touch, units, isIntegerOnly, hasClear.

Calendar API surface: ISODateString template-literal type, min/max/dateConstraints, min/maxRangeSpan, weekStartsOn as a number or 'mon', a `calendar` system prop, and range presets. This matters for your ar and other locales.
Table as data plus columns plus headless plugin hooks (sort, selection, pagination, filtering, sticky columns, column resize, row expansion, tree, grouping) for admin panels.
Three distinct cards (Card, ClickableCard with label and href, SelectableCard with isSelected and onChange) instead of one overloaded card.

Theme tokens as [light, dark] tuples compiled to light-dark(). Map your Material 3 roles at the leaves instead of keeping two palettes. A suggested mapping (my inference): --color-accent/--color-on-accent ↔ primary/on-primary; --color-background-surface ↔ surface; --color-border ↔ outline-variant; --color-border-emphasized ↔ outline; --color-error-muted/--color-on-error-muted ↔ error-container/on-error-container.
Motion tokens with min/base/max per tier and theme knobs (tempo, character), plus the pointer-aware reduced-motion rule (instant on fine pointers, a 200ms or shorter fade on touch).

Docs as data: a per-component doc file (props, do/don't, WCAG checks, anatomy, theming targets) that generates your docs pages, a catalog, and an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md index. This is the web counterpart of the catalog app in your Compose design system.
Page templates as a deliverable alongside components (dashboard, settings, table-page, login, detail page, form wizard, kanban), since that is where most rewriting time goes.
An eject or swizzle command (or a shadcn-style registry) so a project can take full ownership of one component without forking the library.
avoid: Beta and fast churn. Still 0.x ('Currently in Beta'), with ten patch releases from 0.7.0 on 2026-10-13 to 0.7.9 on 2026-11-06 plus hundreds of canary builds, and 732 open issues. Pin exact versions and expect codemods (astryx upgrade --apply).

Browser support for overlays. Full fidelity needs Chrome or Edge 125+, Safari 26+ and Firefox 147+ for CSS anchor positioning. Safari 17–18 users fall into 'Tier 2', where tooltips, menus and popovers may not sit next to their trigger (docs/browser-support). This is a real risk for public user panels with older iPhones. Radix plus Floating UI is safer today.
StyleX is a required peer (@stylexjs/stylex ^0.19.0) even if you only consume prebuilt CSS. xstyle overrides and source builds tie you to StyleX, which conflicts with a Tailwind/cva-first library.
Install weight: @astryxdesign/core is about 28 MB unpacked with 4,610 files (npm dist metadata). Subpath imports keep bundles smaller, but the dependency is large.
Runtime themes inject component overrides after hydration and flash under SSR (docs/theme). Use `theme build` output. For static-export sites, that means a build step for the theme.
Cascade-layer ordering is fragile: if a theme stylesheet loads before globals.css declares the layer order, Tailwind preflight overrides Astryx base styles (docs/styling-libraries).

Token vocabulary differs from Material 3 (accent, background-surface, text-primary versus primary, surface, on-surface). Adopting it as-is would split your role-name convention shared with the Compose app. Map at the leaves; never copy raw hex values into a second theme.
Locale gap: component strings ship in 30 locales but not id, th or sw (three of your 18). Those fall back to English for built-in strings such as 'Loading'.
Copying source is legal under MIT with Meta's notice, but the StyleX styles would need a full rewrite to Tailwind and cva. Treat it as an API and behaviour reference rather than paste-ready code.

Docs pages are client-rendered (component pages fetched here returned only navigation). The canonical reference is the CLI and the *.doc.mjs files in the repo. llms.txt tells agents to run `npx @astryxdesign/cli`.
Do not reuse the Astryx name or branding: MIT grants no trademark rights.
fit:
For your Tailwind v4 + cva + Radix + motion stack, Astryx is most valuable as a source of API conventions and component behaviour, not as code to paste. Its prop grammar, async-action Button, Field contract, Calendar/NumberInput semantics, Table plugin hooks, data-attribute theming and LinkProvider are worth reproducing in your own library. Copying is allowed under MIT with Meta's notice.

It could also be used directly as a dependency in internal admin panels. Your older project already used @astryxdesign/core with StyleX. Prebuilt CSS plus the Tailwind v4 bridge means no build plugin, and React 19 is already your baseline.

It is a weak fit for these cases:
- Static-export marketing sites: runtime themes flash, and the 28 MB package is heavy.
- Public user panels where older Safari matters: overlays rely on anchor positioning.
- A library that must stay Tailwind and Material 3 role-name first: StyleX peer and a different token vocabulary.

It offers no marketing or visual-effects components. Use it for the admin and app UI layer, and take effects and marketing blocks from the other references.

name: HeroUI v3 (formerly NextUI)
oneLiner: An open-source React 19 component library (Apache-2.0, v3.2.7) built on React Aria Components and Tailwind CSS v4. Its styles ship as framework-agnostic BEM CSS plus tailwind-variants functions, and a separate paid HeroUI Pro tier adds the app-shell and dashboard components.

The license also has a patent-termination clause and grants no trademark rights, so do not use 'HeroUI' in your library's name. Older v2 code (branch v2) is MIT ('Copyright (c) 2020 Next UI Inc.'), which only requires keeping the notice. HeroUI Pro (heroui.pro) is different. Its terms (last updated 19 Mar 2026) say you may not 'share, publish, redistribute, or sub-license HeroUI Pro components' or 'create or distribute a tool, library, or service that competes with HeroUI Pro'. Pro components therefore cannot go into any library, open or private, that you distribute. Apache code can live inside an MIT project as long as those files keep their Apache terms. The cleaner choice is to license the new library Apache-2.0, which also matches the user's Compose design system. One practical conflict: the 4(b) modified-file notice clashes with the cosum-web 'no comments in code' rule. Decide up front whether ported files get a license header or whether a THIRD_PARTY/NOTICE list is enough; whether a list alone satisfies 4(b) is unverified.

stack.framework: React 19+ only (peer react >=19.0.0). Every component file starts with "use client". There is also a separate React Native library (heroui-native).
stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (peer tailwindcss >=4.0.0). Component styles are plain CSS files with BEM classes and @apply (packages/styles/components/button.css). tailwind-variants 3.3.1 (MIT, also maintained by heroui-inc) only maps props to BEM classes, and twMerge is off by default (packages/react/src/utils/tv.ts). Themes are CSS custom properties in oklch, wired into Tailwind with @theme inline (packages/styles/themes/shared/theme.css). Hover and soft colours are derived with color-mix(in oklab).
stack.headlessPrimitives: React Aria Components (peer react-aria-components ^1.22.1, react-aria ^3.53.1, @internationalized/date). There are two small exceptions: @radix-ui/react-avatar 1.3.1 for Avatar and input-otp 1.5.0 for InputOTP.
stack.animation: CSS only. The v3.0.0 notes say 'Every animation moved to CSS'. tw-animate-css 1.4.0 (a dependency of @heroui/styles) drives entering and exiting through [data-entering]/[data-exiting]. v2's framer-motion peer dependency is gone (npm @heroui/react@2.8.10 peers vs 3.2.7). Reduced motion is handled with motion-reduce: plus a global [data-reduce-motion="true"] switch.
stack.other: No provider is required (frameworks docs). I18nProvider, RouterProvider, getLocalizationScript, useLocale and isRTL are re-exported from RAC (packages/react/src/components/rac/index.ts). Agent tooling: llms.txt, a .mdx version of every docs page, an MCP server, AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md. The heroui CLI handles init/install/upgrade. There is a Theme Builder at /themes.

distribution: npm packages: @heroui/react 3.2.7 (about 958 KB unpacked, 438 files) and @heroui/styles 3.2.7 (about 1.1 MB unpacked; holds the CSS and the tv variant functions, can be used without React). You import it in CSS with '@import "tailwindcss"; @import "@heroui/styles";', or selectively per base, theme or component file. The heroui CLI does init, install, upgrade, agents-md and design-md. This is not a shadcn-style copy-paste registry. HeroUI Pro is installed through the licensed heroui-pro CLI and needs an account.

standout.name: Button (+ ButtonGroup)
standout.why: A clean model for a semantic-variant button. Variant classes only set component CSS variables, and the press feedback is tuned per size. It shows how to drop asChild in favour of a render function.
standout.apiNotes: Source: packages/react/src/components/button/button.tsx, packages/styles/src/components/button/button.styles.ts, packages/styles/components/button.css. Props: variant 'primary'|'secondary'|'tertiary'|'outline'|'ghost'|'danger'|'danger-soft' (default primary). There is no separate color prop; v2's color×variant matrix was removed. size 'sm'|'md'|'lg' (default md), fullWidth, isIconOnly, isDisabled, isPending, onPress(PressEvent). children can be a function receiving {isPending,isPressed,isHovered,isFocused,isFocusVisible,isDisabled}. render(props, renderProps) replaces asChild, which was removed in beta.3. There is no built-in spinner: you compose <Spinner color="current" size="sm"/> through the children function. startContent/endContent were removed; icons go in as children and CSS auto-sizes any svg. CSS: .button sets --button-bg, --button-bg-hover, --button-bg-pressed and --button-fg, and each .button--{variant} only overrides those variables. Pressing scales to 0.97 (sm 0.98, lg 0.96). Heights are h-10 by default and md:h-9 from the md breakpoint, so buttons are taller on phones. States are exposed as data-hovered, data-pressed, data-focus-visible and data-pending. ButtonGroup passes size, variant, isDisabled and fullWidth through context, but only to direct children, marked with a BUTTON_GROUP_CHILD prop. To style a Next Link as a button: className={buttonVariants({variant, size})}. Custom variants: tv({extend: buttonVariants, variants: {radius: {...}, size: {xl: ...}}}).

standout.name: Card + Surface (SurfaceContext)
standout.why: Close to M3 surface-container levels. A container announces its surface level through context so the controls inside can pick a contrasting style. It is also a textbook tailwind-variants slots component.
standout.apiNotes: Source: packages/react/src/components/card/card.tsx, surface/surface.tsx, packages/styles/src/components/card/card.styles.ts. cardVariants = tv({slots: {base:'card', header:'card__header', title:'card__title', description:'card__description', content:'card__content', footer:'card__footer'}, variants: {variant: {default|secondary|tertiary|transparent}}}). The root computes the slots once and puts them in a CardContext. Each part calls slots.header({className}) and sets data-slot="card-header". Parts: Card.Header, Card.Title (h3), Card.Description (p), Card.Content, Card.Footer. Each part accepts render to swap the element through dom.<tag>. Every non-transparent Card wraps its children in a SurfaceContext. Surface variant is default|secondary|tertiary|transparent (bg-surface, bg-surface-secondary, bg-surface-tertiary). Overlays such as the Select popover reset the context to 'default'. The docs tell you to use variant="secondary" for Input/TextArea placed on a surface.

standout.name: NumberField (counter / stepper)
standout.why: An accessible increment/decrement counter with Intl number formatting (percent, currency, units), validation and keyboard/wheel support. The open-source answer to the 'counter' component; HeroUI Pro sells a fancier 'Number Stepper'.
standout.apiNotes: Source: packages/react/src/components/number-field/number-field.tsx, number-field.styles.ts. Anatomy: <NumberField><Label/><NumberField.Group><NumberField.DecrementButton/><NumberField.Input/><NumberField.IncrementButton/></NumberField.Group><Description/><FieldError/></NumberField>. The buttons are RAC Buttons with slot="increment"/"decrement" and default plus/minus icons you can replace. Slots: base, group, input, incrementButton, decrementButton. Variants: variant primary|secondary, fullWidth. RAC props it inherits: value/defaultValue/onChange, minValue/maxValue, step, formatOptions (Intl.NumberFormatOptions; the docs use {style:'percent'}), isDisabled, isInvalid, validate. Docs: https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/number-field.mdx

standout.name: Calendar / RangeCalendar / DatePicker / DateRangePicker
standout.why: Fully composable, localised calendars with week/day views, a year picker, unavailable dates and event-dot indicators. Radix has no equivalent, and it covers the user's 'calendar' requirement directly, including Arabic and Hijri-style calendar systems.
standout.apiNotes: Anatomy: Calendar > Calendar.Header (Calendar.Heading, Calendar.NavButton slot="previous"|"next") + Calendar.Grid > Calendar.GridHeader {(day)=>Calendar.HeaderCell} + Calendar.GridBody {(date)=>Calendar.Cell date={date}}. Calendar.Cell children can be a function of {formattedDate,isSelected,isUnavailable,isDisabled,isOutsideMonth}; add <Calendar.CellIndicator/> for event dots. Props: selectionMode 'single'|'multiple', value/defaultValue/onChange, minValue/maxValue, isDateUnavailable, firstDayOfWeek, visibleDuration {months|weeks|days} (week and day views were added in v3.2.0), pageBehavior, weeksInMonth, and year-picker parts (YearPickerTrigger, YearPickerGrid visibleYears, YearPickerCell). Uses @internationalized/date (CalendarDate, ZonedDateTime). Docs: https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/calendar.mdx

standout.name: Toast
standout.why: A sonner-style imperative API on top of an accessible queue: stacking with expand-on-hover, a promise helper, in-place updates and a keyboard hotkey. A good fit for admin save flows.
standout.apiNotes: toast('msg'), toast.success, toast.info, toast.warning, toast.danger, toast(msg, {description, variant, timeout, onClose, actionProps:{children,onPress}, indicator, isLoading}). toast.update(id, msg, {variant, timeout}) keeps the toast's position in the stack. toast.promise(p, {loading, success:(d)=>..., error}). Queue methods: add, update, close, pauseAll, resumeAll, clear, subscribe, plus wrapUpdate (for example document.startViewTransition) and exitDuration. Toast.Provider props: placement 'top start'..'bottom end' (logical start/end), gap 12, maxVisibleToasts 3, scaleFactor 0.05, width 460, hotkey ['altKey','KeyT'], isExpanded. Parts: Toast.Content, Toast.Indicator, title/description. Variant: default|accent|success|warning|danger. Docs: https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/toast.mdx

standout.name: Sheet (new in 3.2.7)
standout.why: A swipeable bottom/side sheet that uses native CSS scroll snapping for snap points instead of a JS physics library such as vaul. Useful for mobile-first user panels.
standout.apiNotes: Anatomy: Sheet > Sheet.Trigger, Sheet.Backdrop > Sheet.Content > Sheet.Dialog > (Sheet.Handle, Sheet.CloseTrigger, Sheet.Header > Sheet.Heading, Sheet.Body, Sheet.Footer > Sheet.Close). Root props: isOpen/defaultOpen/onOpenChange, onClose, onAnimationEnd(open), placement 'bottom'|'top'|'left'|'right' (physical edge), isDismissable, isDetached (inset from the edges), snapPoints (number|string)[]. Sheet.NestedRoot is for stacked sheets. Backdrop variant: 'opaque'|'blur'|'transparent'. Dialog role: 'dialog'|'alertdialog'. Docs: https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/sheet.mdx

standout.name: Table
standout.why: The open-source admin data table: sorting, selection, expandable rows, column resizing, virtualization, async load-more, an empty state, and a documented TanStack Table integration.
standout.apiNotes: Anatomy: Table > Table.ScrollContainer > Table.Content(aria-label) > Table.Header > Table.Column ... Table.Body > Table.Row > Table.Cell, plus Table.Footer. Extra parts: Table.SortableColumnHeader, Table.ColumnResizer, Table.ResizableContainer, Table.LoadMore/LoadMoreContent, Table.Collection, and TableLayout/Virtualizer re-exported from RAC. Variants include 'secondary'. Example sections: Async Loading, Sorting, Selection, Expandable Rows, Pagination, Column Resizing, Empty State, Virtualization, TanStack Table, Custom Cells. The Pro 'Data Grid' (inline cell editing etc.) is paid. Docs: https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/table.mdx

standout.name: Tabs
standout.why: A sliding active indicator with no JS animation library. It is React Aria's SelectionIndicator animated with CSS transitions on translate, width and height, and an overflow-scrolling list container.
standout.apiNotes: Anatomy: Tabs > Tabs.ListContainer > Tabs.List(aria-label) > Tabs.Tab > (Tabs.Separator?, Tabs.Indicator), then Tabs.Panel. Props: variant 'primary' (filled pill) | 'secondary' (underline), orientation horizontal|vertical, align start|center|end (v3.2.5), plus RAC selectedKey/onSelectionChange. CSS (packages/styles/components/tabs.css): .tabs__indicator {transition-property: translate, width, height; 250ms var(--ease-out-fluid)} with motion-reduce:transition-none.

standout.name: Theme token system (themes/shared/theme.css + Colors docs)
standout.why: Not a component, but the most transferable idea. You define only the base roles and derive hover, soft and soft-foreground with color-mix. This maps almost one-to-one onto M3 state layers and the user's role names.
standout.apiNotes: Base tokens: --background/--foreground, --surface, --surface-secondary and --surface-tertiary (+ -foreground), --overlay, --muted, --default, --accent, --success, --warning, --danger (each with -foreground), --field-*, --border, --separator, --focus, --link, --radius, --field-radius, --surface-shadow, --overlay-shadow. Derived: --color-accent-hover = color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 90%, var(--accent-foreground) 10%), --color-accent-soft = color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 15%, transparent), soft-hover 20%, soft-foreground = var(--accent), background-secondary/tertiary = background mixed with 4% or 8% foreground. Exposed to Tailwind through @theme inline as --color-*, so bg-surface-secondary and text-accent-foreground work. Themes switch on [data-theme="x"] plus a class. Global behaviour tokens: --skeleton-animation shimmer|pulse|none, --tooltip-delay, --cursor-interactive, --disabled-opacity.

buttonApi: The only visual axis is a single semantic `variant`: 'primary'|'secondary'|'tertiary'|'outline'|'ghost'|'danger'|'danger-soft'. There is no `color` prop; v3 removed v2's color+variant matrix (solid/bordered/light/flat/faded/shadow) and `radius`. Other props: `size` 'sm'|'md'|'lg', `fullWidth`, `isIconOnly` (square; needs aria-label). States: `isDisabled` and `isPending` (loading). Loading has no built-in spinner: you render <Spinner/> through the children function `({isPending, isPressed, isHovered, isFocused, isFocusVisible, isDisabled}) => ...`. v2's isLoading/spinner/spinnerPlacement are gone. Events use React Aria's `onPress` (not onClick). Icons are plain children, and CSS sizes them automatically (startContent/endContent were removed). Polymorphism: asChild was removed in beta.3. Use `render={(props, renderProps) => <button {...props}/>}`, which must keep the same element type and forward the ref, or style any element or Next Link with `buttonVariants({variant, size, isIconOnly})` or the BEM classes `button button--primary`. Groups: `<ButtonGroup>` provides size, variant, isDisabled and fullWidth to direct children through context. Extension: `tv({extend: buttonVariants, variants: {...}})` in a wrapper component. Sources: packages/react/src/components/button/button.tsx and https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/button.mdx.
apiPatterns: Every multi-part component supports three equivalent syntaxes: dot notation (<Card.Header>), an explicit .Root (<Card.Root>), and flat named exports (CardRoot, CardHeader). The named exports were added for React Server Components (v3.0.0-alpha.35; composition docs).

One tailwind-variants tv() per component with `slots`. The root computes the slots once with useMemo and shares them through context, and each part calls slots.part({className}). A custom root can call the slots by hand (linkVariants().base()).

BEM classes are the public styling API (.card__header, .button--primary, .button--icon-only). Overrides go in `@layer components {}`, and the classes work on any element or framework (@heroui/styles can be used without React).

Each variant class only sets component-scoped CSS variables (--button-bg, --button-bg-hover, --button-bg-pressed, --button-fg), and the base class consumes them. Variants stay tiny and are trivially overridable.

data-slot on every part (data-slot="button", "card-header", "number-field-increment-button", "spinner") lets parent CSS target children without class coupling. Example: button svgs exclude [data-slot=spinner].

State is exposed as data attributes and CSS fallbacks: [data-hovered], [data-pressed], [data-focus-visible], [data-pending], [data-entering]/[data-exiting], [aria-expanded]. Hover styles sit inside @media (hover:hover) so touch devices do not get sticky hover.

A `render` prop (DOMRenderProps, adapted from RAC; packages/react/src/utils/dom.tsx) replaces asChild. A `dom` Proxy (dom.div, dom.h3) creates cached elements, and in dev it warns if the ref was not forwarded.
RAC render props everywhere: children and className can be functions of state (composeTwRenderProps in utils/compose.ts).

SurfaceContext: containers (Card, Surface) announce their surface level, overlays reset it, and form controls are told to use variant="secondary" on a surface. This is the same idea as M3 surface-container tiers.
Context from a group to its children applies only to direct children (a BUTTON_GROUP_CHILD marker prop), so nested buttons do not inherit by accident. Explicit props always win over context.
Accessibility comes from React Aria: keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA, and localised strings for about 34 locales. Focus rings are keyboard-only.

RTL: logical CSS properties (v3.2.3), toast placements written as 'top start'/'bottom end', and isRTL/useLocale/I18nProvider re-exported. The frameworks docs show an I18nProvider in a client provider for Next.js locale matching.

Reduced motion: every transition is followed by `motion-reduce:transition-none` (the CSS comments stress the order matters), and the variant also honours [data-reduce-motion="true"] on html/body as a global kill switch.

Theming uses [data-theme] plus a class and next-themes. Base colour roles come in pairs (x / x-foreground), and hover/soft tokens are derived with color-mix(in oklab). Themes are imported into `layer(theme)`.
Mobile-first touch sizing: the default control is h-10 and shrinks to md:h-9 on wider screens.

Docs are written for agents: each page has Anatomy → Examples → Customization → CSS classes → Interactive states → API tables → Render props, and is served as raw .mdx (/en/docs/react/components/button.mdx). There are also llms.txt/llms-full.txt, an MCP server, AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md.
borrow: Port the token-derivation idea onto the existing M3 roles rather than adopting HeroUI's names. Keep primary/on-primary/surface-container-low and so on from theme.css, and generate hover, pressed and focus 'state layers' with color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 92%, var(--on-primary) 8%) and similar. M3's 8%/10% state-layer opacities fit this formula exactly, so Compose and web stay in lockstep without new hex values.

Use the per-component CSS variable pattern for the Button: the base reads --ds-button-bg/-hover/-pressed/-fg and each variant only sets them. Name the variants after M3 (filled, tonal, outlined, text, elevated, plus danger/danger-tonal) so they match the Compose DSButton. Sizes sm/md/lg.
Adopt tailwind-variants (MIT, has slots, compoundSlots and `extend`) for multi-part components (Card, NumberField, Calendar, Table). Keep cva for single-element ones if you like; cva has no slots.

Export the variant function (dsButtonVariants) next to every component, so a next-intl `Link` from @/i18n/navigation can be styled as a button without nesting <a><button>. This fits the cosum-web rule that Link must come from @/i18n/navigation.
Put data-slot on every part, and drive state through data attributes such as data-pressed and data-pending, so consumers can restyle without extra props.

Offer a children-as-function render prop for state ({isPending, isPressed}) and a `render` prop for element swapping instead of asChild. Pick one polymorphism API for the whole library and document it.

Copy the SurfaceContext idea using M3 tiers. <DSCard level="container-low"> provides its level and DSTextField picks the contrasting container automatically, matching how Compose's LocalContentColor/tonal elevation works.

Use the RAC-backed date, number and calendar stack, either directly or through HeroUI's compositions, for the admin and user panels. Radix has no Calendar, DatePicker or NumberField, and RAC brings Arabic RTL, Hijri and other calendar systems, and Intl number formatting.
Copy the toast API shape: toast(), toast.success/danger, toast.promise, and toast.update(id) that keeps the stack position, with logical 'top start'/'bottom end' placements for RTL.
For mobile user panels, copy the Sheet's snapPoints via native CSS scroll-snap, avoiding a JS drag-physics dependency.

Tune press feedback per size (scale 0.98 for sm, 0.97 for md, 0.96 for lg), keep transform-gpu, put motion-reduce after every transition, and add a global [data-reduce-motion] switch. This complements cosum-web's existing data-reveal/noscript rule.

Use the docs structure for each component's catalog page (Anatomy, Examples, CSS hooks, States, API table, Render props), and serve a raw .mdx/llms.txt so Claude can read the library's own docs. This mirrors the Compose catalog app.
Use the docs' table of prop-to-intent mappings (v2 color+variant to v3 variant) as a model for writing a migration table when MUI and Astryx/StyleX projects move onto the new library.
avoid: HeroUI Pro is paid and off limits for any library you distribute. The pieces an admin panel needs most (AppLayout, Sidebar, Navbar, Data Grid, KPI, KPI Group, Kanban, Number Stepper, Number Value, Charts, Command, Stepper, Rich Text Editor, Agenda, Timeline) are Pro-only (heroui.pro/llms.txt). The terms forbid redistribution and building a competing library (heroui.pro/terms, 19 Mar 2026). Do not copy from Pro docs or examples.

The open-source v3 removed Navbar (https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/migration/navbar.mdx says to build it by hand). There is no app shell or sidebar in the free set, so the layout components have to come from your own work or other MIT sources.

Generic global class names: @heroui/styles defines unprefixed .button, .card, .link, .input, .surface, .header, .table and so on. Importing the whole stylesheet into an existing site restyles any element that already uses those names. If you port the BEM approach, prefix it (for example .ds-button), consistent with the Compose 'DS' prefix.

Do not mix stacks carelessly. HeroUI is built on React Aria while the user's sites use Radix. Running both means two focus-management, portal and dismiss systems plus z-index fights. Choose RAC or Radix per primitive family and note it in the library README.
RAC naming (onPress, isDisabled, isOpen/onOpenChange, isPending) differs from DOM and Radix naming (onClick, disabled, open/onOpenChange). Settle the convention before the first component.

React Aria ships built-in translated strings (button labels such as previous/next, clear, etc.) for 34 locales. id, vi, th and sw are missing and fall back to English; I checked adobe/react-spectrum packages/react-aria/intl/calendar. Four of the 18 cosum locales would need overrides. Date and number formatting still uses Intl, so those parts work.

Every component is a client component ("use client"). On static-export marketing pages, a plain BEM class or buttonVariants on a native element is lighter than hydrating a RAC Button. Bundle cost per component is unverified: the npm unpacked sizes are about 958 KB (@heroui/react) and 1.1 MB (@heroui/styles), not gzip numbers.

Breaking churn inside v3 minors: Text was renamed to Typography in 3.0.5, Radio/Checkbox/Switch composition broke in 3.2.0, and dependency declarations changed in 3.2.6. Pin exact versions if you depend on it directly.
Button has no built-in loading spinner or isLoading convenience, so a wrapper is needed if the team wants the one-prop `isLoading` behaviour they had in MUI or HeroUI v2.

Apache-2.0 notice duties (keep 'Copyright 2025 NextUI Inc.' and mark modified files) clash with the 'no comments in code' convention. Settle how ported files are attributed before copying any v3 source.
The default theme is a zinc/oklch look with rounded-3xl buttons. Adopting it as-is would drift away from the Compose port, so remap tokens to the M3 roles instead of overriding colours case by case.
fit: The closest stack match of the reference sites: React 19, Tailwind v4, a variant-function system (tailwind-variants, much like cva but with slots), CSS-only motion, RTL-aware, and no provider, so it works with Next 15 static export. The best use is as an architecture and pattern source plus a selective donor for app-side components: the token derivation, per-component CSS variables, slots, data-slot, render props and SurfaceContext, and the RAC-based Calendar, DatePicker, NumberField, Table, Toast and Sheet for the admin and user panels. Copying open-source v3 code into an Apache-2.0 library is allowed with attribution. It is a weaker fit as a direct dependency for the marketing sites: every component is a client component, the global unprefixed BEM classes may collide, the tokens are HeroUI-named rather than M3, and it brings React Aria alongside the Radix already in use. It is no help for the app shell (Navbar, Sidebar, KPI tiles, Data Grid), because in v3 those exist only in the paid, non-redistributable HeroUI Pro. Effects and flashy blocks should come from other sources; HeroUI is about solid, accessible primitives.

oneLiner: Bencho is a catalogue of 161 interactive React micro-interaction blocks and Web Audio interface sounds. 46 blocks and 24 sounds are free under MIT in a GitHub repo, where each block is a folder you copy. standout.name: Dynamic island (blocks/dynamic-island/Island.tsx)
standout.why: The source of the 'one shape, swapped content' morph. It suits a live status pill in an admin or user panel: upload progress, sync, a running timer or a call. The pill grows as one object instead of a box whose corners catch up later.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: activity ('Timer'|'Call'|'Music'|'Flight', default 'Timer'), bounce (0–100, default 40), tone ('Black'|'White'), startOpen (default true). The README documents only tone and bounce.

How it animates: one motion.button animates width, height and borderRadius on a single spring {stiffness 380, damping 34 - b*16, mass 0.9}. Each activity has its own open size (Timer 300×76 r38, Music 300×150 r42, Flight 300×116 r40); closed it is 150×36 r18. Content swaps through AnimatePresence mode="popLayout", keyed on `${kind}-${open}`, with a {opacity, scale .92, blur 6px} crossfade (0.22s, 0.06s delay). A separate wrapper keyed on a nudge counter gives a 1.08 swell when the activity changes, so it does not fight the size spring. whileTap scale .97. aria-expanded and aria-label 'Open/Close <kind>'.

Problems: inner controls are <span role="button" tabIndex=0> with only onClick (no Enter/Space) nested inside the <button>, which is invalid interactive nesting. The content is hard-coded demo data with English strings, the CSS uses hex colours and left/right, and ART points at '/lab/mount.jpg'.

standout.name: Rolling counter (blocks/rolling-counter/Counter.tsx)
standout.why: An odometer number stepper. It fits a quantity or number field, a KPI that animates when it changes, and a 'counter increment' component. No framer-motion: it runs a hand-tuned rAF spring.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: bounce (default 45), stagger (0–120 ms, default 45), blur (0–100, default 50), corner (0–28 px, default 16), start (default 95). Each digit column targets floor(value/10^p), so 9→10 rolls the ones column forward and carries instead of spinning back. Columns move in turn, ones first. Velocity-proportional motion blur on the digit strips.

The knob is mapped through springOf(): k = 0.08 + t*0.16 and decay d = 0.62 + t*0.2, chosen so the damping ratio runs from about 0.85 to 0.20.

Input: holding a button repeats after 380 ms, then every 90 ms, then 55 ms, and steps by 10 after 1.5 s. You can also drag the number vertically (12 px per step) and fling it. role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow/min/max and ArrowUp/ArrowDown.

Gaps: uncontrolled (no value/onChange/min/max/step), PLACES=5 is fixed, the ',' separator is hard-coded, and the aria labels are English.

standout.name: One-time code (blocks/one-time-code/Otp.tsx)
standout.why: A correct OTP technique plus a striking verify animation. Good for auth screens.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: length (4|6), answer ('Accept'|'Reject', which only simulates the server result), corner (0–22). One invisible <input> sits over drawn cells, so paste, SMS autofill, backspace and screen readers all work. The input has inputMode="numeric", autoComplete="one-time-code", maxLength=n, and data-1p-ignore / data-lpignore / data-bwignore / data-form-type="other" to keep password managers out.

Verify animation: a goo filter from a useId-scoped useGoo(blur, cut) hook merges the cells into a 'Verified' capsule on an underdamped spring (k 0.075, damping ratio 0.42). A rejected code shakes the row with a decaying sine and drains the digits. The caret stretches with its own speed.

Gap: no onComplete or async verify callback.

standout.name: Liquid toggle (blocks/liq-toggle/Toggle.tsx)
standout.why: The best worked example of a velocity-driven squash with framer-motion motion values. It would make a good 'SwitchV2' look on top of a Radix Switch.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: speed (default 50) and stretch (default 36). Motion chain: x = useMotionValue, then useVelocity(x), then useSpring(vel, {380, 34, mass .6}), then useTransform into scaleX = lengthen(v)*swell and scaleY = swell/lengthen(v). That keeps the thumb's area constant. The code explains why the hover swell is multiplied into the transform rather than set with the CSS `scale` property (the scale property applies before transform and shifts the translate).

A press that never moved counts as a click and toggles. role="switch", aria-checked, Space/Enter.

Gaps: uncontrolled, aria-label is fixed to 'Liquid toggle', and it assumes left-to-right translateX.

standout.name: Slide to confirm (blocks/slide-confirm/SlideConfirm.tsx)
standout.why: A reference for a destructive-action confirmation, such as deleting an account in an admin panel. The handle widens into a 'Confirmed' pill.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: width (220–380, default 280), corner (0–28), speed (0–100). Width is computed with useTransform([seen, anchor]) from the motion value the spring already moves, so the corner radius never scales. Further useTransform chains drive label fade, overdrag squash and arrow opacity.

Gaps: no keyboard path at all (no onKeyDown or onClick on the handle) and no onConfirm callback.

standout.name: Toast stack (blocks/toast-stack/ToastStack.tsx)
standout.why: A Sonner-style stack that fans out on hover or focus. Useful for admin notifications.
standout.apiNotes:
Real props: peek (6–24 px), gap (4–20 px), corner (0–32). Each toast's place comes from place(k, open) and is driven by one spring {380, 34, mass 1}. Uses pointerover/pointerout with a containment test rather than pointerenter/leave, and opens on focus. role="region" with aria-label. Tucked toasts get aria-hidden and tabIndex=-1. data-kind sets the colour of each kind (success/info/error/warning).

Gaps: a hard-coded POOL of demo toasts, no toast() imperative API, no aria-live, English copy.

standout.name: Magnetic select (blocks/magnet-select/MagneticSelect.tsx)
standout.why: A chip or segmented single-select where the chosen chip swells and pushes its neighbours away. A tasteful filter control.
standout.apiNotes: Real props: size ('Small'|'Large', i.e. 3 or 7 options), pull, bounce, give (all 0–100). role="radiogroup" with radio children and aria-checked. A comment explains that the chosen chip moves an indicator and applies forces while the layout itself never moves.

standout.name: Checklist (blocks/checklist/Checklist.tsx)
standout.why: Checkbox motion: the box fills, the tick draws in and the text strikes through. Good for onboarding or progress cards.

Real props: corner (0–40), box (14–28 px), bounce (0–100). Its own useSpring(target, tune, instant) hook. role="checkbox" with aria-checked. AnimatePresence handles leaving rows.

Gap: TASKS is a hard-coded English array.

standout.name: Sounds (sounds/sounds.ts)
standout.why: 24 interface sounds with no audio files. A sound is plain data, which is easy to port into an opt-in package.
standout.apiNotes: play(name: SoundName, {volume?, pitch?}) creates the AudioContext lazily and resumes it on a user gesture. SOUNDS maps names to Note[] arrays, where Note = {hz, to?, glide?, ms, gain?, wave?, cut?, at?, atk?, noise?: 'bandpass'|'lowpass', q?, lin?}. schedule(ctx, notes, when, volume, bend) is exported, so sounds can also be rendered offline.

standout.name: Like (blocks/like/Like.tsx)

standout.apiNotes: Real props: start (count, default 1300), effect ('Bloom'|'Firework'), burst (0–100), color ('Red'|'Ink'), corner. Uses aria-pressed. The digits roll through AnimatePresence mode="popLayout" with a 40 ms stagger per digit. Formatting is hard-coded to toLocaleString('en-US').

buttonApi: There is no Button primitive. No free block takes variant, size, color, loading, icon, asChild or group props, and there is no shared Button. The free set has only special-purpose pressables: 'Escape button' (corner, skittishness, patience, radius) is a joke button that dodges the cursor, and 'Like' is a toggle with aria-pressed and a rolling count. The Pro blocks 'Pay button' (spinner morphing to success) and 'Sweep button' (animated gradient border) are Pro-licensed; I did not inspect them and they cannot go into a library. Across the catalogue, props are 'feel knobs' (corner, bounce, speed) rather than design-system variants. Use it for ideas for an expressive ButtonV2 (press squash, success morph), not for the button API.
apiPatterns: Motion props are 'feel knobs' on a 0–100 scale (bounce, speed, stretch, pull, give, burst). A documented formula turns them into spring constants: pick the damping ratio first, then derive stiffness and decay. 50 is the tuned default and both ends stay usable (Counter.tsx springOf()).

Every prop is optional and defaults to what the live demo shows. Each block's README has a table 'Prop | Knob | Default | Range | What it does' and a section 'Tokens it reads' listing the CSS variables the block depends on.

Theming goes only through semantic CSS custom properties in tokens.css. Dark mode applies under [data-theme="dark"] on any ancestor, or follows prefers-color-scheme unless [data-theme="light"] is set. The token file says to map its names onto your own theme rather than keep two token sets.

State is styled through data-* attributes (data-on, data-phase, data-kind, data-tone, data-held, data-done, data-front) rather than class toggles. This maps directly onto Tailwind v4 data-[on]: variants.
Reduced motion is respected: a stillness() check makes springs {duration:0} and loops snap to the end. 13 of the 14 blocks inspected do this; ToastStack does not.

Hand-rolled springs stay correct when frames drop, because dt is measured in 60ths of a second and the damping is raised to the power dt rather than multiplied by it. The rAF loop stops once the value settles, so nothing keeps running.

Shape and content are animated separately: container size and radius ride one spring, while content swaps through an AnimatePresence popLayout crossfade with blur and scale. Secondary effects such as the nudge swell sit on their own wrapper so they do not fight the main spring.
SVG filter ids come from useId(), so two instances on one page do not steal each other's goo filter.

ARIA roles are written by hand: switch, spinbutton (arrow keys), radiogroup/radio, checkbox, region. Hidden stacked items get aria-hidden and tabIndex=-1. The OTP field carries attributes that keep password managers out.

A per-block 'Copy prompt' button and an MCP server let a coding agent fetch a component with its CSS, packages and current settings. Worth copying for the user's own library, e.g. llms.txt plus a registry plus an MCP.
borrow: Use the 0–100 feel-knob idea on top of the user's own motion tokens. For example a `bounce` or `speed` prop, or a MotionPreset provider, converted to motion springs through the damping ratio, with 50 as the house default. This keeps expressive variants such as ButtonV2 and SwitchV2 tunable without exposing stiffness and damping.
Adopt the per-component docs table: Prop | Default | Range | Description | Tokens it reads. Generate it from TypeScript types for the catalogue site, in the spirit of the Compose catalog app.

Build a StatusPill or LiveActivity component on the Dynamic island technique: one spring on width, height and radius, plus an AnimatePresence popLayout crossfade. Rewrite the API with open/onOpenChange, compact and expanded slots (children), real nested buttons, and next-intl strings. Use it for uploads, sync state and timers in admin and user panels.

Rebuild the rolling counter as a controlled NumberField or Stepper (value, onValueChange, min, max, step, formatOptions). Keep the column-carry odometer, the stagger, hold-to-repeat acceleration and drag-to-change. Format with Intl.NumberFormat(locale) so tr, de and ar separators and digits are right. Reuse the digit roller as a standalone AnimatedNumber for KPI cards.

OTP: keep the single-hidden-input structure and its attributes (inputMode numeric, autoComplete one-time-code, password-manager ignore attributes, useId filter ids). Add onComplete(code) and an async status prop (idle, checking, success, error) to drive the merge and shake.
Switch: keep Radix Switch for semantics and add the useVelocity → useSpring → useTransform squash as a 'liquid' variant. Flip the x direction when dir is rtl.
Toast: adopt the fan-out stack's look (peek, gap, a single spring, fan out on hover or focus) on an imperative toast() API with aria-live. Sonner's model works for this.
Sounds: ship an opt-in @yourlib/sounds package modelled on sounds.ts (Note[] data, lazy AudioContext, play(name, {volume, pitch})). Keep it off by default and controlled by a user preference.

Map Bencho's tokens onto Material 3 roles once when porting: --ink → on-surface, --ink-3 → on-surface-variant, --card or --surface → surface-container-low, --surface-2/3 → surface-container/-high, --fill-slab → surface-container-highest, --pane-edge → outline-variant, --signal or --focus → primary, --ok → a custom success role. Never carry Bencho hex values over.
Keep a THIRD_PARTY.md that names every MIT source file you adapted. Bencho's own THIRD_PARTY.md, which credits cuelume, is a good template.
avoid: Never copy Pro blocks into the library, private or open source. That is about 115 of the 161, including Pay button, Sweep button, Dropdown, FAQ accordion, Resizable panels, Collapsing sidebar, Tab bar, Date reel, Skeleton morph and the AI chat input. The Pro licence bans 'a UI kit, component library, template… snippet collection' and 'a library, service or MCP server that hands blocks to other people'. It is also one licence per person, so teammates using a shared internal kit would each need Pro. Take code only from the MIT GitHub repo.
Do not use the 'Bencho' name, the goat mark or the bencho.dev photos. None of them are licensed. The Maison Neue font is not bundled either.

Do not treat the blocks as primitives. They are self-contained demos: no value/onChange, no children or slots, no className, no ref forwarding, no asChild. Demo data and English copy are hard-coded (the toast POOL, Checklist TASKS, Upload SNARK messages, fake upload files, flight and music content). Every port is a rewrite of the API.

They are not ready for i18n or RTL, and the user ships 18 locales including Arabic. Number formatting is hard-coded toLocaleString('en-US') and aria labels are English. The CSS uses 31 physical left/right declarations and no logical properties in the 14 blocks read, and the transforms assume left-to-right translateX.
Hard-coded colours (136 hex values in the 14 CSS files read, e.g. the island's #000, #30d158 and #e09a12) clash with the 'no hex outside theme.css' rule. Port them to M3 roles.

Accessibility gaps to fix, not copy. The Dynamic island nests <span role=button> controls with only onClick inside a <button>. Slide to confirm has no keyboard path. Toast stack has no aria-live. Reduced motion is read once at render rather than live.
There are no 'use client' directives, and the blocks touch window and matchMedia. Under the Next App Router each needs 'use client' and must not render differently on the server and the client.
Global per-block CSS files with prefixed class names do not fit a Tailwind v4 + cva library. Convert them to Tailwind utilities or CSS modules rather than shipping .dyn-* globals.

Imports use framer-motion. The user's projects use `motion`, so switch to motion/react (same API). One block depends on three.js (Folding bill) and one on liquid-gooey (Dragging ball), which are heavy for an admin kit.
Source files carry long essay comments, some mentioning the author's own CLAUDE.md and lab/ paths. Strip them when porting; the user's convention is no code comments.
The npm package 'bencho' belongs to someone else (a benchmarking CLI by mrmlnc), and llms.txt's 'The blocks are MIT licensed' is outdated. Do not rely on either.
fit:
Partial fit. Bencho is a source of effects and micro-interactions and a reference for motion code, not a source of primitives. The overlap is real: React 19, TypeScript and framer-motion, which is the same API as the user's `motion` package. The mismatches are large: plain global CSS and Bencho's own tokens instead of Tailwind v4 with M3 roles, no Radix or cva, uncontrolled demo components without slots, and no RTL or i18n.

Best role: an 'expressive' layer built on the user's own Radix + cva primitives. Candidates are SwitchV2 (liquid), AnimatedNumber/NumberField (rolling counter), OtpField, StatusPill (dynamic island), ToastStack styling, SlideToConfirm and an opt-in sounds module. Each is reimplemented against M3 roles and next-intl, with an MIT notice for the adapted files.

Licence fit: the 46 free blocks may be copied into an MIT or Apache open-source library with the MIT notice kept. The ~115 Pro blocks must never go into it.
