stack.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn CSS variables (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, border-input, accent). Older items carry a tailwind.config.js extension, which the registry route converts into shadcn cssVars and keyframes. Many community items hardcode zinc, neutral or indigo colours.
stack.headlessPrimitives: Mostly Radix (@radix-ui/react-slot, radix-ui). Newer items also use Base UI (@base-ui/react, e.g. extend-hq Button) and React Aria (shadcn's 'aria' base). Others use react-day-picker for calendars, TanStack Table v9 with dnd-kit for data grids, and the HeroUI v3 packages.
stack.animation: motion (motion/react) or framer-motion in most animated items (Motion Primitives, Magic UI, Aceternity). Number Flow uses the Web Animations API inside a custom element. Some items use tw-animate or CSS keyframes injected through registry 'css'.
stack.other: The platform uses Supabase, Clerk and Cloudflare R2 (old README). Its agent surface is llms.txt, a .md twin for every page, an OpenAPI 3.0 spec (https://21st.dev/openapi.json), an MCP server at https://21st.dev/api/mcp and SKILL.md skills. Newer side products: Design Bug Bot (design review on PRs), Remotion video blocks, an open-source apps directory, and the 21st Agents SDK.

distribution:
A marketplace and registry, not a package. You can install a component four ways:
(1) shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add "https://21st.dev/r/<user>/<slug>?api_key=$API_KEY_21ST"`. Without a key, a live test of /r/shadcn/button returned HTTP 403 {"error":"Authentication required"}.
(2) 21st CLI: `npx @21st-dev/cli@latest` provides `21st search`, `21st get` (prints code and demo), `21st add <user>/<slug>` (runs shadcn under the hood) and `21st add @team/slug`.
(3) 21st MCP: `npx @21st-dev/cli@latest init --client <cursor|claude|codex|vscode|devin>` writes the config for the HTTP MCP at https://21st.dev/api/mcp with an `x-api-key` header. The legacy `@21st-dev/magic` package is now a stdio proxy to the same server.
(4) Copying the TSX, or using "Copy prompt" for an agent, on the web.

How a registry item is built, from serafimcloud/21st apps/web/app/api/r/[username]/[component_slug]/route.ts: it outputs standard shadcn registry-item JSON. That means a type mapping (ui→registry:ui, blocks→registry:block, hooks→registry:hook, icons→registry:ui), npm `dependencies`, recursively resolved `registryDependencies` and the `files` array. It also outputs `cssVars` taken from the component's globals.css and `css`/`cssVars.theme` (animations and keyframes) parsed from its Tailwind config. Paid items are checked against purchases.

Publishing: Studio on the web, `21st` CLI drafts, or `POST /components/publish`. Publish metadata includes `license`, `registry` (ui|hooks|blocks|icons), `runtime` (react|expo), `demos[]` with light and dark preview images and videos, and visibility. Review states are on_review → posted → featured.

Private team registries: `npx @21st-dev/registry` (MIT), with a 21st.json manifest, component.tsx, demos/default.tsx and preview.png. Visibility is --unlisted, --public or --private, and --to <registry> picks the target. Hosting is on 21st.

Pricing (https://21st.dev/pricing.md): Free gets 2 copies a day. Builder is $6/mo yearly or $8/mo quarterly and unlimited. Builder + AI is $15–60/mo for 500–2,000 credits. Team is $7.50 or $18.75 per seat. Templates are bought per template.
componentCount: 12,000+ community components across components, templates, themes, icons and hooks (https://21st.dev/llms.txt, https://21st.dev/mcp.md). Examples of tag sizes: the Button tag says "250" and lists 200; Calendar says "78"; Number/counters lists 40; the Aceternity UI library has 89 components on 21st.
categories: Marketing sections: hero, features, CTA, pricing, testimonials, footer, landing pages
Navigation: navbar, sidebar, tabs
Core UI: buttons, button groups, cards, dialogs, forms, inputs, tables, tooltips, avatars, badges, accordion, carousel, marquee
Dashboard and admin: stats cards, bento grids, data grid tables, charts, dashboard shells, rate-limit meters
Calendars and date pickers: react-day-picker calendars, full-screen and event calendars, booking
Numbers and counters: Number Flow, sliding number, number ticker, count-up, countdown
Auth/login and AI chat (plus the separate Agent Elements registry)
Motion: animated components, text animation, backgrounds and shaders
Hooks, icons, animated icons and SVG logo search
Themes (shadcn CSS variable themes), templates (some paid), Remotion video blocks, open-source app starters

standout.name: Button (shadcn, @shadcn/button: canonical shadcn v4 source in shadcn-ui/ui apps/v4/registry/bases/{radix,base,aria}/ui/button.tsx)
standout.why: This is the baseline every other 21st button copies. The v4 version splits structure from look: the TSX only emits semantic classes (cn-button, cn-button-variant-outline, cn-button-size-sm), and per-style CSS files (style-vega.css, style-nova.css, style-maia.css…) map those classes to Tailwind with @apply. One API can therefore ship several visual 'styles' without forking the component, which is the cleanest way to get a 'ButtonV2'.
standout.apiNotes: cva variants are default|outline|secondary|ghost|destructive|link. Sizes are default|xs|sm|lg|icon|icon-xs|icon-sm|icon-lg. It renders data-slot="button", data-variant and data-size. The Radix base uses `asChild` with Slot.Root. The Base UI base takes `ButtonPrimitive.Props`, using Base UI's `render` composition. The React Aria base splits into Button and a separate LinkButton. The style CSS uses in-data-[slot=button-group] and has-data-[icon=inline-start|inline-end] for padding when an icon is present. Licence MIT (shadcn-ui/ui).

standout.name: ReUI Button ('button-1' on 21st by @sean0205: v1 source at keenthemes/reui commit a02a2d9, registry/default/ui/button.tsx)
standout.why: The richest real Button API on 21st and a good model for a filled/tonal/outlined/text matrix. It also handles the 'button that opens a popover/select' case.
standout.apiNotes: variant: primary|mono|destructive|secondary|outline|dashed|ghost|dim|foreground|inverse. appearance: default|ghost. mode: default|icon|link|input, where `input` makes the button look like a select trigger with invalid and open ring states. size: lg|md|sm|xs|icon. radius: md|full. Also underline and underlined (solid|dashed), autoHeight, placeholder (muted text), and `selected`, which sets data-state="open". There are 46 compoundVariants, and `asChild` uses Radix Slot. A `ButtonArrow` sub-part uses logical ms-auto and -me-1, which is RTL-safe. Defaults: variant primary, mode default, size md, radius md. Current ReUI main has moved to the slimmer shadcn-v4 style (variant and size only). Licence MIT.

standout.name: Texture Button (cult-ui, @cult-ui/texture-button: nolly-studio/cult-ui apps/www/registry/default/ui/texture-button.tsx)
standout.why: Shows the two-layer 'bevel' button: an outer cva for the gradient border shell and an inner cva for the surface. A good reference for a decorative ButtonV2. It is also a cautionary example.
standout.apiNotes: variant: primary|secondary|accent|destructive|minimal|icon. size: default|sm|lg|icon. `asChild` via @radix-ui/react-slot, and React.forwardRef. Problems found in the source: zero focus-visible styles ('focus' appears 0 times in the file); a hardcoded indigo/red/neutral palette; `w-full` on every variant; and `asChild` is effectively broken, because Slot receives the internal <div> wrapper rather than the consumer's element. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Number Flow (@barvian/number-flow: npm @number-flow/react 0.6.2, repo barvian/number-flow)
standout.why: The best counter on the site for an 18-locale, RTL, accessibility-conscious library. It formats with Intl.NumberFormat, sets an accessible label through ElementInternals (ariaLabel = valueAsString), respects reduced motion, and has no runtime dependencies besides its own core.
standout.apiNotes: Props: value; locales (Intl.LocalesArgument); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); prefix and suffix; trend (a number or (old, new) => sign); animated; respectMotionPreference; transformTiming, spinTiming and opacityTiming (EffectTiming); digits (per-position max, e.g. for clocks); plugins (e.g. continuous); isolate; willChange; onAnimationsStart and onAnimationsFinish. `NumberFlowGroup` syncs several numbers. Hooks: useCanAnimate, usePrefersReducedMotion, useIsSupported. Peer deps react ^18 || ^19. Licence MIT. Better used as a dependency than ported.

standout.name: Sliding Number (Motion Primitives, @ibelick/sliding-number: ibelick/motion-primitives components/core/sliding-number.tsx)
standout.why: Small, readable example of per-digit spring animation with motion's useSpring, useTransform and layoutId. Good for learning, not for copying as-is.
standout.apiNotes: Props: value, padStart (bool), decimalSeparator (default '.'). Deps: motion and react-use-measure. Each digit renders 10 absolutely positioned spans driven by a spring (stiffness 280, damping 18, mass 0.3). Gaps: no aria-label or sr-only value, so screen readers meet 10 numbers per digit; no Intl or locale digits; no reduced-motion handling. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Number Ticker (Magic UI, @dillionverma/number-ticker: magicuidesign/magicui apps/www/registry/magicui/number-ticker.tsx)
standout.why: The popular 'count up when scrolled into view' stat. Useful to see which traps to avoid in a static-export marketing site.
standout.apiNotes: Props: value, startValue (0), direction (up|down), delay (seconds), decimalPlaces, plus span props. Uses useInView({ once: true }) and useSpring (damping 60, stiffness 100), and writes textContent directly. The source shows the traps: `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")` is hardcoded; the server/static HTML renders `startValue`, so a no-JS or SEO view shows 0; colours are hardcoded text-black and dark:text-white; there is no reduced-motion support. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Data Grid Table (ReUI, @sean0205/data-grid-table: keenthemes/reui registry-reui/bases/radix/reui/data-grid/*)
standout.why: The most complete admin-panel table among the 21st items reviewed here, on TanStack Table v9 and dnd-kit. It has an i18n label object, which fits next-intl, and start/end naming, which fits RTL.
standout.apiNotes: DataGrid props: table, recordCount, isLoading, loadingMode ('skeleton'|'spinner'), loadingMessage, emptyMessage, onRowClick, i18n (DataGridI18nOverrides: sortAscending, pinColumnStart, pinColumnEnd, rowsPerPage, loading, empty…), tableClassNames, and tableLayout {dense, cellBorder, rowBorder, stripped, headerBackground, headerBorder, headerSticky, width 'auto'|'fixed', columnsVisibility, columnsResizable, columnsPinnable, columnsMovable, columnsDraggable, rowsDraggable, rowsPinnable}. columnDef.meta takes headerTitle, skeleton, expandedContent, headerColSpan, fillWidth and cellEdit {editable, parse, format, clearValue, control 'text'|'textarea'}, with spreadsheet-style onCellsChange. Separate files cover pagination, column filter, column visibility, scroll area, DnD rows and columns, and a virtual table. `dataGridFeatures` is the TanStack v9 feature bundle. The file opts out of React Compiler with 'use no memo'. The source has heavy comments, which you would strip under a no-comments convention. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Calendar [React Day Picker] (Origin UI, @originui/calendar: cosscom/ui apps/origin/registry/default/ui/calendar.tsx)
standout.why: A clean token-driven skin over react-day-picker. It is a good template for a date picker that has to follow next-intl locales and RTL.
standout.apiNotes: Takes all `React.ComponentProps<typeof DayPicker>` and merges per-slot `classNames` (day_button, range_start, range_middle, range_end, today, outside, nav, weekday…) with the user's overrides. `components` can override the Chevron. Styling keys off data-selected, data-disabled and data-outside, and range ends use logical rounded-s and rounded-e. The today dot combines start-1/2 with a physical -translate-x-1/2, which is unverified in RTL. Locale and dir have to be passed through DayPicker props. Licence MIT (cosscom/ui, formerly origin-space/originui).

standout.name: Event Calendar (Origin UI: cosscom/ui apps/origin/registry/default/components/event-calendar/*)
standout.why: A full month, week, day and agenda scheduler with drag-and-drop. A useful starting point for logged-in user panels.
standout.apiNotes: EventCalendarProps: events, onEventAdd, onEventUpdate, onEventDelete, className, initialView ('month'|'week'|'day'|'agenda'). CalendarEvent: {id, title, description?, start, end, allDay?, color?, location?}. EventColor: 'sky'|'amber'|'violet'|'rose'|'emerald'|'orange'. Split into month-view, week-view, day-view, agenda-view, event-dialog and DnD context files, with window keydown shortcuts. Not ready for i18n: 'Today' is hardcoded English, date-fns `format` is called without a locale, `weekStartsOn: 0` is hardcoded, and colours are raw palette names rather than roles. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Animated Background (Motion Primitives: ibelick/motion-primitives components/core/animated-background.tsx)
standout.why: The shared-layout 'sliding highlight' behind segmented controls, tabs and nav items, a very common dashboard flourish.
standout.apiNotes: Props: children (elements carrying `data-id`), defaultValue, onValueChange(id|null), className (for the moving pill), transition (motion Transition), enableHover. It uses cloneElement to inject data-checked and handlers, and a motion.div with layoutId from useId. Gaps: activation is click or hover only, with no keyboard model and no role or aria-selected. A better approach is a motion layoutId indicator inside Radix Tabs or ToggleGroup. Licence MIT.

standout.name: Agent Elements (21st-dev/agent-elements, a separate shadcn registry at agent-elements.21st.dev)
standout.why: 26 MIT components for AI or assistant panels, built for React 19, Tailwind v4 and the Vercel AI SDK, the same stack you use.
standout.apiNotes: From the README only (component props unverified): AgentChat (MessageList + InputBar + tool dispatch); tool cards BashTool, EditTool (diff and approval), SearchTool, TodoTool, PlanTool, ToolGroup, McpTool, ThinkingTool; QuestionTool; composer parts InputBar, Suggestions, ModelPicker, ModeSelector, SendButton, AttachmentButton; streaming Markdown, TextShimmer, SpiralLoader. Install with `npx shadcn@latest add https://agent-elements.21st.dev/r/agent-chat.json`. Files land in components/agent-elements/.

buttonApi:
There is no single 21st Button. The Button tag holds about 250 author-submitted buttons, and each has its own API. The two worth modelling are:
(1) The canonical shadcn v4 Button: cva `variant` default|outline|secondary|ghost|destructive|link and `size` default|xs|sm|lg|icon|icon-xs|icon-sm|icon-lg. It emits data-slot, data-variant and data-size, and composes with `asChild` (Radix Slot), with `render` (Base UI base) or through a separate `LinkButton` (React Aria base). Visual styles live in separate CSS files that map `.cn-button-variant-*` with @apply. Loading is not a prop; the shadcn examples nest a Spinner (spinner-button.tsx).
(2) ReUI v1 Button: `variant` (10 values), `appearance` default|ghost, `mode` default|icon|link|input, `size` lg|md|sm|xs|icon, `radius` md|full, underline and underlined, autoHeight, placeholder, `selected` (sets data-state=open), asChild, 46 compoundVariants, and a `ButtonArrow` sub-part.
Other examples on 21st: cult-ui TextureButton (two-layer cva, variants primary|secondary|accent|destructive|minimal|icon); HeroUI v3 ButtonGroup (MIT); extend-hq Button (Base UI with a built-in loading state through a Spinner; upstream source not located, so unverified); shugar 'Split Button' from a Geist port (licence 'unknown').
apiPatterns: Data attributes as the styling API: data-slot on every part plus data-variant and data-size (shadcn v4, ReUI). Parents style children with selectors like in-data-[slot=button-group]:rounded-md or has-data-[icon=inline-start]:ps-2, with no extra props.

Structure and style kept apart: the TSX emits semantic classes (cn-button-variant-outline) and each 'style' CSS file maps them with @apply (shadcn-ui/ui apps/v4/registry/styles/style-*.css). Several looks share one component API.

One API over interchangeable headless bases: the same Button exists for Radix (asChild/Slot), Base UI (render prop) and React Aria (Button + LinkButton) under shadcn apps/v4/registry/bases/{radix,base,aria}.

Large cva matrices with compoundVariants (ReUI: variant × appearance × mode × size, 46 compound rules), with `selected` mapped to data-state=open so a trigger button and an open popover share styling.
Sub-part components for slots, such as ReUI ButtonArrow using logical ms-auto and -me-1, so RTL works without extra props.
Per-slot classNames merging over a headless engine (Origin Calendar merges user classNames into DayPicker's slot map; ReUI DataGrid has tableClassNames).
An i18n label object prop with defaults plus overrides (ReUI DataGridI18nOverrides). It plugs straight into next-intl `t()` and uses start/end naming instead of left/right.
Locale-aware, accessible numbers: Intl.NumberFormat with a `locales` prop, an aria label set through ElementInternals, and respectMotionPreference and useCanAnimate (Number Flow).

shadcn registry item contract: `dependencies` (npm) vs `registryDependencies` (other items, resolved recursively); type registry:ui, block, hook or lib decides the target folder; `cssVars` (theme/light/dark) and `css` (keyframes) inject tokens and animations at install time.

Component plus demos convention: one reusable component file, with demos that exercise it only through props, and a light and dark preview image or video per demo (21st README quality guidelines; 21st.json in 21st-dev/registry).

Agent-facing docs: llms.txt, a .md twin of every page (also served for Accept: text/markdown), an OpenAPI spec, an MCP server (search is free metadata, get_component is metered code retrieval) and SKILL.md skills, so coding agents can find and install components.
borrow: Ship your own library as a shadcn-compatible registry. registry.json goes through `npx shadcn build` to produce public/r/*.json, which any static host can serve, including the Apache/Hostinger setup you already run. Install becomes `npx shadcn add https://<your-domain>/r/<item>.json`. Namespace file names so your button does not overwrite theirs, use `registryDependencies` to chain your own items, and use `cssVars` to carry your Material 3 role tokens.

Implement ButtonV2 as a style layer rather than a fork. Keep one Button with data-variant and data-size, and map M3 variants (filled, tonal, outlined, text, elevated) to classes in a theme CSS file, as shadcn's style-*.css files do. A different look then becomes a second CSS mapping.

Take ReUI v1's extra Button axes that admin panels need: mode='input' (button as a select trigger with invalid and open rings), `selected`, which sets data-state=open, and a ButtonArrow sub-part with logical margins. Add an explicit `loading` prop that renders a spinner and sets aria-busy, which shadcn leaves to composition.

Use Number Flow (@number-flow/react, MIT) as a dependency for counters, stats and KPI tiles. Pass the next-intl locale to `locales`. Do not port SlidingNumber or NumberTicker; both lack locale support and an accessible value.

Base the admin data table on ReUI DataGrid's API (tableLayout flags, meta.cellEdit, loadingMode, i18n overrides) on TanStack Table, feeding the i18n object from next-intl. Strip upstream comments to match your no-comments rule.

Wrap react-day-picker the way Origin UI does (per-slot classNames merge, Chevron override), and add `locale` and `dir` from next-intl, plus a locale-aware weekStartsOn. Origin's Event Calendar is a reasonable starting point for user panels once the strings and date-fns locale are injected.

Copy 21st's authoring convention for your catalog: component.tsx plus demos/<name>.tsx plus light and dark previews, with demos driven only by props. It matches the Compose catalog app you already have.

Use 21st as a search index only. Find a candidate, open the author's upstream GitHub repo, check its LICENSE, and copy from there. Record each third-party piece in a NOTICE or THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES file, because MIT only needs the notice shipped with copies and your rules forbid code comments.

Make your library agent-friendly cheaply: an llms.txt, a .md twin per component doc page, and later a small MCP or SKILL.md, so Claude Code and Cursor install your components instead of rewriting them.

Bridge token names once. Alias shadcn names (primary-foreground, muted, accent, border, input, ring) to your M3 roles in theme.css, so MIT components pasted from upstream inherit your palette without per-file edits.
avoid: Copying code out of 21st.dev itself into an open-source repo. The ToS limits use to 'solely through the official 21st.dev platform' and forbids redistributing, selling or licensing marketplace content without authorization. Copying to any other medium needs a visible link back. Scraping and AI-training uses are prohibited without written consent.

Items whose licence field reads 'unknown', e.g. the Aceternity UI components (89 on 21st) and shugar's Geist 'Split Button'. Aceternity's own licence forbids redistributing source files regardless of modifications, so treat these as inspiration only.

Building a workflow that depends on 21st retrieval. Registry URLs now return 403 without an API key, free accounts get 2 copies a day across Web, MCP and CLI, MCP `get_component` is metered, 21st AI `generate` needs paid credits, and some templates are sold per item.

Hardcoded palettes (zinc, neutral, indigo, red in Texture Button; sky, amber, violet colour names in Event Calendar). They bypass your Material 3 roles and break the 'no hex or raw colour outside theme.css' rule.

Locale and RTL traps in popular items: `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")` hardcoded in Magic UI NumberTicker; English 'Today', date-fns format without a locale and weekStartsOn: 0 in Origin's Event Calendar; physical translate-x and pl/pr utilities in some styles. Audit each item for ar/RTL before adopting it.

Accessibility gaps. Texture Button has no focus-visible style, and its asChild is broken by an inner div. SlidingNumber exposes 10 spans per digit to screen readers. AnimatedBackground uses cloneElement with click or hover only, no keyboard support and no ARIA state.
Counters that render their start value on the server. In a static export, NumberTicker's HTML shows 0 until JS runs, so render the final value and animate from it.
Treating serafimcloud/21st as current. It was last pushed in May 2025, its README describes Next.js 14 and Sandpack, and the live service (API-key gating, Design Bug Bot, video blocks) has diverged.

Uneven community quality. Anyone can publish, and items in on_review are reachable by direct link, so a review only happens before an item is featured. Check props, tokens, dark mode and licence one item at a time.
Tailwind v3-era items that rely on a tailwind.config.js extension. The registry converts these into cssVars and keyframes, which can clash with a Tailwind v4 @theme setup.
fit: Good fit as a discovery index and as a model for distribution. It is not a direct source of code. Most items share your stack: React 19, Tailwind, cva, Radix and motion. Their token names are shadcn's (primary-foreground, muted, accent), so you would need one alias layer onto your Material 3 roles. Roles: (1) Inspiration and search: finding candidate components, then taking the MIT code from the upstream repos. The richest of those are ReUI for admin needs (Button, DataGrid, statistics cards), Origin UI/coss for calendars and inputs, Motion Primitives and Magic UI for motion, and Number Flow for counters. (2) A distribution model for your own library: the shadcn registry format runs fine on a static host, which matches your static-export setup, and 21st-dev/registry is a hosted option for private team registries. (3) Optional later: publishing your open-source library to 21st as a library listing to get discovered, since authors keep authorship. Weak fit as an install source for production projects, because of API-key gating, daily quotas, ToS limits on redistribution, uneven i18n and RTL handling, and accessibility gaps in popular items.

name: React Bits
oneLiner: A free catalogue of 218 animated, copy-in React components (text effects, cursor and hover effects, cards and galleries, "Micro" interaction controls, WebGL backgrounds). Each comes in four flavours (JS or TS, CSS or Tailwind) and installs through a shadcn or jsrepo registry. It is not an npm package or a design system.
maker: David Haz (GitHub DavidHDev), the solo maintainer, with community fixes. Funded by sponsors and a paid "React Bits Pro" tier. CONTRIBUTING.md says new community components are not accepted, only enhancements and fixes.
stars: 51,350 stars and 2,575 forks (gh api repos/DavidHDev/react-bits, read 2026-11-06)
lastActivity: Last commit 2026-10-31 ("🎃"); the ones before it are 2026-10-19 "add landing updates" and 2026-10-18 "New: Center Stage + Sound Lab". The repo has no GitHub releases and package.json version is 0.0.0.

license.name: MIT + Commons Clause License Condition v1.0, a custom text in LICENSE.md. GitHub shows it as NOASSERTION/'Other'. It is not an OSI open-source license.
license.restrictions: 1) The grant is narrower than MIT. Use, copy, modify, merge, publish and distribute are allowed only 'as part of an application, website, or product', and the copyright and permission notice must be kept in all copies. 2) Commons Clause: commercial use is allowed as long as you 'do not sell, sublicense, or redistribute the components themselves', whether alone, in a bundle, or as a ported version. 3) The same applies to the React Bits tools (Background Studio, Texture Lab, Shape Magic, Center Stage, Sound Lab) and the sound library, which also may not be offered as a hosted service. Tool exports may be used in apps but may not be sold or redistributed on their own, for example as a texture or background pack. 4) The README credit section says some components draw inspiration from publicly available code examples, so where they came from is not fully documented. 5) llms.txt says everything on reactbits.dev is 'free and open source', which is misleading next to the Commons Clause. 6) React Bits Pro is a separate paid license: $129 / $249 / $349 one-time, or $79 / $149 / $199 per year. It covers one developer for unlimited commercial projects, and its terms say the code cannot be repackaged as a competing component library or template (pro.reactbits.dev/llms.txt). WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE USER: (a) Pasting or installing a component into one of their own Next.js sites or admin panels, commercial included, is allowed as long as the notice stays. (b) Putting React Bits code, or a ported or restyled version, into a component library published under MIT or Apache, or put on npm, is NOT allowed, because that redistributes the components 'in a bundle' or 'as a ported version'. (c) A private internal package used only by their own apps is a grey area. It is arguably still 'part of a product', but it must never be published or shared. (d) Re-implementing an interaction idea from scratch in their own code, without copying source, is fine for an open-source library.
license.evidence: https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits/blob/main/LICENSE.md (read via gh api repos/DavidHDev/react-bits/contents/LICENSE.md). The deciding sentence: you may use the software commercially as long as you do not sell, sublicense or redistribute the components themselves, alone, in a bundle or as a ported version. The permission clause limits copying and distribution to doing so 'as part of an application, website, or product'. The README badge also reads 'MIT + Commons Clause'.

stack.framework: The components target React 19 (package.json react ^19.0.0). All 24 component files I sampled start with 'use client', so they work in the Next.js App Router as client components. The docs site itself is Vite + react-router-dom + Chakra UI and is served from Cloudflare (worker/, wrangler.jsonc). It is not Next.js.
stack.styling: Four parallel variants of every component: JS-CSS (src/content), JS-TW (src/tailwind), TS-CSS (src/ts-default), TS-TW (src/ts-tailwind). Each folder holds 218 files. The Tailwind variants assume Tailwind v4 and lean on long arbitrary-value classes and data-* variants. Each component has its own CSS custom-property namespace fed from props (--hb-* in HoldButton, --fb-* in FuseButton, --gs-* in GlideSelect, --rs-* in RubberSegment). Some components inject a raw <style> string, for example HoldButton's STYLE constant with masks and keyframes.
stack.headlessPrimitives: None. There is no Radix, React Aria or Base UI. ARIA is hand-rolled: role=switch (SquishSwitch), combobox+listbox+aria-activedescendant (GlideSelect), radiogroup/radio (RubberSegment), slider (ElasticSlider), spinbutton (ScrubField), menu/menuitemcheckbox (Dock), tooltip (WarmTooltip), listbox/option (AnimatedList).
stack.animation: motion/react (useReducedMotion, useSpring, useMotionValue, animate) in 10 of the 24 sampled TS-TW files. GSAP + ScrollTrigger in AnimatedContent and FadeContent. standout.name: HoldButton (Micro)
standout.why: A ready-made pattern for destructive actions in admin panels: hold to confirm instead of a modal. It works from the keyboard, has a reduced-motion fallback, and exposes its state machine as data attributes.
standout.apiNotes: Props from src/ts-tailwind/Micro/HoldButton/HoldButton.tsx: children (default 'Hold to delete'), doneLabel, icon, doneIcon, size 'sm'|'md'|'lg', radius=14, fillDirection 'right'|'up', holdTime=2000, releaseTime=200, pressScale=0.97, wave, waveAmplitude, glow, resetAfter=1200, disabled, onHold, onTap, className. Colours are raw strings (backgroundColor '#27272a', fillColor '#5227FF', textColor, fillTextColor) piped into --hb-* CSS variables. The root carries data-phase (idle/holding/done), data-input (pointer/key), data-direction and data-glow. It handles onKeyDown/onKeyUp, links a hint with aria-describedby, and uses contrast-more: and focus-visible: styles. There is no rest-spread and no ref.

standout.name: FuseButton (Micro)
standout.why: An action button with an undo window: it commits after a visible countdown and can be undone in the meantime. A good fit for archive and delete actions in admin tables, and its callbacks report why they fired.
standout.apiNotes: label/undoLabel/doneLabel, icon, size 'sm'|'md'|'lg', radius=22, undoWindow=4000ms, fuse 'outline'|'bottom'|'top', fuseThickness, crossfadeMs, commitOn 'press'|'fuseEnd', pauseOnHover=true, settle 'reset'|'stay', disabled, type 'button'|'submit'|'reset'. Callbacks: onCommit(reason: FuseCommitOn), onUndo, onFuseEnd, onPhaseChange(phase: 'idle'|'armed'|'settled'). Accessibility: sr-only role=status aria-live=polite, aria-keyshortcuts='Escape' on undo, and a forced-colors: fallback for the fuse.

standout.name: SlideCommit (Micro)
standout.why: Shows how to drive a loading state from the action's own Promise: the button enters pending, then done or error, without a separate loading prop.
standout.apiNotes: onConfirm?: () => void | Promise<unknown>. If the result is thenable, the phase goes 'idle' → 'pending' → 'done' | 'error', and onDone and onError(reason) fire. Labels: label/doneLabel/errorLabel as ReactNode. Colours: trackColor, handleColor, successColor, dangerColor. Also width, height, radius, holdMs, icon. Uses motion's useReducedMotion.

standout.name: Counter (Components)
standout.why: The strongest dashboard KPI number here. Formatting is fully locale-aware and it renders the locale's own digits (Arabic-Indic for ar) by deriving the glyphs from Intl, which suits 18 locales.
standout.apiNotes: value, locale='en-US' (string|string[]), format: Intl.NumberFormatOptions (currency, percent, compact), decimals, minDigits, prefix/suffix as ReactNode, direction 'auto'|'up'|'down'|'shortest', duration=0.7, bounce, stagger, motionBlur, intro, fade, fontSize, fontWeight, textColor='inherit', tabular=true, digitStyle, className, style. Implementation: digitsFor() asks Intl for the numbering system's glyphs, slotsFor() uses formatToParts, an sr-only span carries the formatted label, and the animated row is aria-hidden. CountUp (TextAnimations) is the simpler sibling: to/from, startWhen, separator string (no Intl locale), mode 'count'|'roll', easing, format 'standard'|'compact', trigger 'view'|'load', replayOnHover, onStart/onEnd.

standout.name: ScrubField (Micro)
standout.why: A numeric field you drag to change and click to type into, with modifier multipliers. It answers the user's 'increment counter' need for admin settings much better than plain +/- buttons.
standout.apiNotes: label, suffix, value/defaultValue, min, max, step, size 'sm'|'md'|'lg', sensitivity, rubberReach (elastic limits), returnDuration, coarseMultiplier (Shift) and fineMultiplier (Alt), showDelta, showDirty, showFill, accent, chipColor, disabled. onChange fires while scrubbing and onCommit on release; the two are deliberately separate. ARIA: role=spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max and inputMode='decimal'. Keys: ArrowUp/Down and PageUp/PageDown.

standout.name: Stepper (Components)
standout.why: A multi-step flow for onboarding and wizards, built as compound components. It has both controlled and uncontrolled modes, a render prop for the indicator and per-part className slots: a good API shape, with i18n and theming gaps to avoid.
standout.apiNotes: <Stepper><Step title description icon>…</Step></Stepper>. Props: step / initialStep / onStepChange, onFinalStepCompleted, indicator 'numbers'|'dots'|'bars', orientation, transition 'slide'|'fade'|'none', linear, disableStepIndicators, renderStepIndicator({step, currentStep, onStepClick}), showFooter, back/next/completeButtonText (defaults 'Back'/'Continue'/'Complete'), backButtonProps/nextButtonProps, completedContent. Slot classNames: stepCircleContainerClassName, stepContainerClassName, contentClassName, footerClassName. Uses aria-current='step' and an aria-live viewport. Gaps: a hardcoded English aria-label `Step ${n}: …`, a theme prop 'dark'|'light' backed by a JS THEMES table, and readableOn(accentColor) that only parses hex, so a CSS var() falls back to white text.

standout.name: GlideSelect (Micro)
standout.why: A compact select chip with a sliding highlight and a correct combobox/listbox ARIA pattern. Its data-state and data-side styling hooks are worth copying.
standout.apiNotes: options: (string | {value, label: ReactNode, tag?})[], value/defaultValue, onChange(value, option), placeholder, showTags, size 'sm'|'md'|'lg', radius, menuWidth, placement 'top'|'bottom', align 'left'|'right' (physical sides, not RTL-aware), popDuration, glideDuration, rememberPosition, disabled, ariaLabel. Colours: accent, surface, highlight and text colour strings. The trigger is role=combobox with aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant; the menu is role=listbox with role=option and aria-selected; styling keys off data-state=open|closed and data-side. There is no `name` prop and no hidden input, so it cannot take part in native form submission.

standout.name: RubberSegment and SquishSwitch / SpringCheck (Micro)
standout.why: Segmented control, switch and checkbox with spring physics from motion. Each has correct roles and a controlled/uncontrolled API, which is a useful reference for the motion layer over Radix-style primitives.
standout.apiNotes: RubberSegment: items, value/defaultValue, onChange(value, index), size, radius, inset, equalSlots, stretch, squash, speed, glide, draggable, disabled, 'aria-label'. It is role=radiogroup/radio with aria-checked; ArrowRight/ArrowDown always moves to the next index, which is not flipped for RTL. SquishSwitch: checked/defaultChecked/onChange(checked), label, ariaLabel, width, height, radius, speed, stretch, hoverScale; role=switch, aria-checked, motion-reduce:. SpringCheck: label, checked/defaultChecked, strike side, bounce, strikeLag, doneOpacity.

standout.name: CodeSlots (Micro)
standout.why: An OTP/verification-code input with paste support and SMS autofill done right. Useful for login and 2FA in user panels.
standout.apiNotes: length, value/defaultValue, onChange(code), onComplete(code), status 'idle'|'error'|'success', mask, caret, autoFocus, disabled, slotSize, gap, radius, bounce/settle/rise/cascade timings, colour props (accent, ink, slot, digit, danger), ariaLabel. The input uses inputMode='numeric' and autoComplete='one-time-code', with an sr-only aria-live count.

standout.name: WarmTooltip + WarmTooltipGroup (Micro)
standout.why: A compound tooltip whose 'warm window' lets a toolbar show the first tooltip after a delay and the neighbouring ones instantly. One of the few React Bits pieces that uses context, forwardRef and child cloning the way asChild does.
standout.apiNotes: WarmTooltipGroup (forwardRef with an imperative WarmTooltipGroupHandle): delay, warmWindow, travel, lean, onWarmChange. WarmTooltip: content, shortcut (a slot for the keyboard hint), children as a single ReactElement trigger (merged through cloneElement, which preserves an existing aria-describedby), side 'top'|'bottom'|'left'|'right', size, arrow, popDuration/popScale/popBlur, showFuse, longPress for touch, disabled. Renders role=tooltip, closes on Escape, and portals through createPortal.

standout.name: SwipeToast and StatusMark (Micro)
standout.why: Feedback pieces for user panels. Their close-reason and status enums are a clean API pattern for toasts and task states.
standout.apiNotes: SwipeToast: title, description, icon, actionLabel/onAction, open, onClose(reason: 'timeout'|'swipe'|'action'|'close'|'escape'|'programmatic'), duration with a fuse 'bottom'|'top'|'none', pauseOnHover, closeButton, dismissible, inline; role=status aria-live=polite; the close button's aria-label 'Close' is hardcoded English. StatusMark: status 'pending'|'running'|'done'|'failed'|'cancelled', progress, label, color/doneColor/errorColor, size, strokeWidth, spinDuration, drawDuration, strike; role=img when it has no label.

standout.name: StarBorder (Animations) / SpotlightCard / AnimatedContent
standout.why: Marketing-site effects: an animated border wrapper, a cursor spotlight card and a scroll-reveal wrapper. StarBorder is the only sampled component that is properly polymorphic.
standout.apiNotes: StarBorder<T extends ElementType = 'button'>: `as?: T` plus Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, own keys>, color, trailColor, duration, thickness, radius, trailLength, stars, glow, sparkle, direction, hover 'lap'|'brighten'|'reveal'|'none', clickPulse, theme 'dark'|'light'. SpotlightCard extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>: spotlightColor, intensity, spotlightSize, softness, shape, borderGlow, proximity, smoothing, ambient, flare, grain, theme. AnimatedContent extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> (GSAP ScrollTrigger): distance, direction, reverse, duration, ease, scale, blur, rotate, tilt, wipe 'none'|'up'|'down'|'left'|'right'|'center', threshold, delay, stagger, staggerFrom 'start'|'end'|'center'|'edges'|'random', trigger 'scroll'|'mount', once, scrub, disappearAfter, onStart/onComplete.

buttonApi: There is no generic Button. Nothing has variant (filled, outline, ghost), color or loading props, and there is no ButtonGroup. React Bits instead ships single-purpose behaviour buttons: HoldButton (hold to confirm), FuseButton (commit with an undo window), SlideCommit (slide to confirm, with Promise-driven pending/done/error), SlingButton (pull-to-send), FlyingButton (a 2,379-line WebGL novelty), SpecularButton (glass shine) and StarBorder (a polymorphic animated-border wrapper). Shared conventions: size 'sm'|'md'|'lg' (HoldButton, FuseButton, SpecularButton); radius as a number in px; colours as raw string props (backgroundColor/fillColor/textColor, tint/baseColor) piped into per-component CSS variables; icon and doneIcon / doneLabel ReactNode slots for the success state; a type 'button'|'submit'|'reset' prop (FuseButton, SpecularButton); internal phase exposed as data-phase for Tailwind group-data-* styling. Only SpecularButton extends ButtonHTMLAttributes and spreads ...rest. HoldButton and FuseButton accept a fixed prop list, so you cannot pass aria-* or data-* through. No sampled button uses forwardRef or takes a ref prop. Polymorphism exists only on StarBorder (`as`), and nothing uses asChild or Slot. Loading exists only as SlideCommit's Promise-returning onConfirm.
apiPatterns: Internal state machines exposed as data attributes (data-phase, data-input, data-direction, data-state=open|closed, data-side, data-on) and styled with Tailwind v4 group-data-[phase=done]: and data-[state=open]: variants. This avoids JS class toggling, and consumers can restyle states from outside.

A scoped CSS custom-property namespace per component (--hb-fill, --fb-fuse, --gs-surface, --rs-thumb) set from props through the style attribute. Colour props are plain strings, so `var(--color-primary)` usually works. Stepper's accent is the exception: readableOn() only parses hex.

Controlled and uncontrolled pairs used everywhere: value/defaultValue/onChange (GlideSelect, RubberSegment, ScrubField, CodeSlots, ElasticSlider), checked/defaultChecked/onChange (SquishSwitch, SpringCheck), step/initialStep/onStepChange (Stepper).
Live updates kept apart from the final value: ScrubField onChange vs onCommit, ElasticSlider onChange vs onChangeEnd, CodeSlots onChange vs onComplete.
Callbacks that say why they fired, as string unions: SwipeToast onClose(reason: 'timeout'|'swipe'|'action'|'close'|'escape'|'programmatic'), FuseButton onCommit(reason) and onPhaseChange(phase).
Promise-aware actions: SlideCommit's onConfirm may return a Promise, and the component derives the pending, done and error phases from it.

Compound components through context (WarmTooltipGroup/WarmTooltip, Stepper/Step), render props (Stepper renderStepIndicator, AnimatedList renderItem), and cloneElement trigger merging that keeps the child's aria-describedby (WarmTooltip).
A polymorphic generic `as` prop typed with ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T> (StarBorder<T extends ElementType = 'button'>).

Reduced motion handled in all 24 sampled TS-TW files, through motion's useReducedMotion, matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'), the Tailwind motion-reduce: variant, or an @media block in injected CSS that swaps the animation for an opacity fade.

Further a11y modifiers: contrast-more: and forced-colors: Tailwind variants (HoldButton, FuseButton), hover gated behind [@media(hover:hover)_and_(pointer:fine)] so touch devices do not get stuck hover, an sr-only role=status / aria-live for state changes, and aria-keyshortcuts.

Hand-rolled ARIA roles with full keyboard maps: switch, combobox+listbox+aria-activedescendant, radiogroup, slider, spinbutton with Shift/Alt multipliers and PageUp/PageDown, menu/menuitemcheckbox, tooltip with Escape.
Locale-correct numbers: Intl.NumberFormat + formatToParts + numbering-system digit glyphs (Counter), with an sr-only formatted label next to an aria-hidden animated row.
'use client' at the top of every component file, so it drops straight into the Next.js App Router.

Registry distribution: one registry item per variant (Name-JS-CSS, Name-JS-TW, Name-TS-CSS, Name-TS-TW) generated by jsrepo.config.ts with the @jsrepo/shadcn output into static public/r/*.json, plus llms.txt and shadcn MCP so agents can install components.

Maintenance tooling: `npm run check:prop-docs` compares scalar defaults across the 4 variants and the docs prop tables (it runs in the production build), and each component's metadata in Information.js carries added and updates: [{date, note}], which feed a per-component changelog.
borrow: Build your own family of behaviour buttons on top of one plain cva Button, re-implemented from scratch against the M3 role tokens: ConfirmHoldButton (from the HoldButton idea) and UndoableActionButton (from FuseButton: an undo window, commitOn 'press'|'timeout', onCommit(reason), onUndo). They fit admin delete and archive flows and avoid confirmation modals.
Let the base Button take an onClick that returns a Promise and derive pending, success and error from it (data-state='pending'), as SlideCommit does, instead of every caller managing a loading flag.
Expose every component's internal state as data-* attributes and style it with Tailwind v4 data variants. This matches the M3 role-token approach and lets an app restyle states without new props.

KPI tiles and counters: use Intl.NumberFormat(locale) + formatToParts + numbering-system digits, with an sr-only text label beside an aria-hidden animated row. This makes Arabic-Indic digits and RTL number formatting work in all 18 locales, and the locale comes straight from next-intl's useLocale().

A numeric admin field in the ScrubField style: value/defaultValue, min/max/step, Shift and Alt multipliers, separate onChange and onCommit, role=spinbutton, inputMode='decimal'. A good basis for the 'increment counter' component.
Typed close and commit reasons on overlays and toasts (onOpenChange(open, reason) or onClose(reason)) so analytics and undo logic know why something closed.
A warm-window tooltip group for admin toolbars. If you already use Radix Tooltip, its Provider's delayDuration/skipDelayDuration covers this, and you only need the shortcut slot idea.
A reduced-motion / contrast-more / forced-colors / hover:hover-gating checklist for every animated component in your library, verified in review the way your i18n:check verifies locales.

Ship your own library as a shadcn-compatible registry: a registry.json plus static /r/{name}.json files (static hosting such as your Apache setup works), a components.json namespace, an llms.txt and shadcn MCP support, so your agents can install your components. Use variant suffixes only if you really need JS/CSS flavours; TS + Tailwind alone is enough for your stack.

Add a prop-docs parity script, like React Bits' check:prop-docs, that fails the build when a documented default drifts from the source, and store per-component {added, updates:[{date, note}]} metadata to generate a changelog in your catalog site, mirroring your Compose catalog app.

Use React Bits components directly (installed with the shadcn CLI) inside individual marketing sites for hero text effects, backgrounds and StarBorder/SpotlightCard flourishes. Keep the license notice, and keep those files in the app repo, never in the shared library.
avoid: License trap: MIT + Commons Clause forbids redistributing the components 'alone, in a bundle, or as a ported version'. Do not copy, port or restyle React Bits code into your planned open-source library, and do not publish it to npm even privately shared. Re-implement ideas from scratch instead. llms.txt calls it 'free and open source', but it is not an OSI license.
Unclear provenance: the README admits some components draw inspiration from publicly available examples. That is another reason not to redistribute them.

Hard-coded hex defaults (fillColor '#5227FF', background '#27272a', and others) and a JS `theme: 'dark'|'light'` prop (Stepper, AnimatedList, Dock, SpotlightCard, StarBorder) instead of CSS tokens and prefers-color-scheme. Both break your 'no hex outside theme.css' and 'role names only' rules, and Stepper's readableOn() turns any non-hex accent into white text.

No RTL handling: none of the 24 sampled files mention rtl or direction. Positioning is physical (left-0, align 'left'|'right'), and RubberSegment maps ArrowRight to the next item regardless of dir, which is wrong for ar.

Hardcoded English accessibility strings: Stepper aria-label `Step ${n}: …`, Dock aria-label 'Dock', SwipeToast close aria-label 'Close', and default 'Back'/'Continue'/'Complete' labels. They would bypass next-intl.

Weak composability: no forwardRef or ref passthrough in sampled components (only WarmTooltipGroup), most do not spread native HTML attributes (HoldButton, FuseButton, GlideSelect), there is no asChild/Slot, and form controls have no `name` or hidden input, so they cannot take part in native form submits or react-hook-form registration without wrapping.
Huge single-file components with long arbitrary-value class strings and injected <style> blocks: FlyingButton 2,379 lines, Dock 1,235, AnimatedList 641. They are hard to maintain and to theme.

Heavy and mixed dependencies: GSAP + ScrollTrigger (Webflow's own 'Standard No Charge' license, not MIT; restriction details unverified) next to motion, plus three, @react-three/fiber, ogl, postprocessing and matter-js for backgrounds. Many are WebGL, so watch bundle size and static-export prerendering.
A second icon set (@hugeicons, MIT) that would be pulled in next to whatever icon set you standardise on.
Pro tier (paid, $129 to $349): its license says the code cannot be repackaged as a competing component library or template, so it is not usable as a source for your library either.
fit: Best role: inspiration and an effects source, not a primitive source. The technology matches your stack well: React 19, 'use client' files, Tailwind v4 classes, and many Micro components built on the same `motion` package you use. You can install individual effects (text animations, backgrounds, StarBorder, SpotlightCard, Counter) into a given Next.js site with the shadcn CLI, keeping the license notice. The Micro category (HoldButton, FuseButton, SlideCommit, ScrubField, CodeSlots, GlideSelect, SwipeToast, StatusMark, WarmTooltip) is the most useful for admin and user panels, as interaction designs to re-implement on your Radix + cva + M3-token primitives. It cannot be the foundation of your library for three reasons: (1) the Commons Clause forbids redistributing the components or ports of them, which rules out an open-source library; (2) the components are not token-driven (hex and theme props), RTL-aware or i18n-clean; (3) they lack ref forwarding, prop spreading and form integration. Copy the distribution model (shadcn registry, llms.txt, MCP, prop-docs check, changelog metadata) and the API patterns (data-phase, controlled/uncontrolled pairs, reason-typed callbacks, Promise-driven pending, Intl-based numbers). Do not copy the code.

stack.framework: React 19.2.4 (ref passed as a prop, no forwardRef). The starter app is Next.js 16.3.3 (package.json). Components are mostly framework-agnostic "use client" files, and the docs list install paths for Next.js, Vite, React Router and Astro.
stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4: @theme primitives, :root semantic tokens, .dark overrides, then @theme inline re-export (styles/theme.css, 565 --color- lines). Custom @utility classes cover the gradient buttons and press motion. @custom-variant gives a class-based dark mode plus rtl/ltr via :dir(). Composite typography utilities follow the pattern text-{family}-{weight} (styles/typography.css). There is no CVA: styles live in plain objects wrapped in an identity helper `sortCx` and are merged with a `cx` built on tailwind-merge's extendTailwindMerge (utils/cx.ts).
stack.headlessPrimitives: react-aria-components ^1.17 (Switch, ToggleButtonGroup, Calendar/RangeCalendar, Popover, Dialog/Modal, NumberField, Slider, Select, Tabs, Tooltip, I18nProvider), plus @internationalized/date. No Radix.
stack.animation: Mostly CSS: @keyframes and @utility in styles/globals.css and theme.css, each with its own prefers-reduced-motion block, and motion-safe: variants on the modal. `motion` ^12.42 is used only in a few places (the DatePicker summary chip, DataGrid rows). The View Transitions API drives the theme reveal. useCountUp is a hand-written requestAnimationFrame hook.
stack.other: Icons are @remixicon/react, passed as component references. Data uses @tanstack/react-table ^8.21 (DataTable) and recharts ^3.9 (chart cards). The agent chat uses the ai SDK v7 with @ai-sdk/*. Inter and JetBrains Mono load via next/font. The starter homepage is a working AI chat on your own model key.

distribution: The main path is copying source into your project, not adding a runtime dependency. `npx boardui@latest init --yes` sets up tokens, globals, the cx helper and AGENTS.md / .cursor rules. `npx boardui@latest add <name>` (or `--all`) installs a component plus its registryDependencies and npm dependencies. standout.name: Button / ButtonLink (components/base/buttons/button.tsx)
standout.why: A clean, small variant × size matrix where the component renders and sizes the icons itself, so a caller cannot pass a wrong-sized icon. The press motion and gradient hover are CSS-only utilities, and an anchor twin covers navigation.
standout.apiNotes: Props: variant: 'primary'|'secondary'|'ghost'|'danger' (default primary); size: 'medium'(36px)|'small'(32px)|'xs'(24px); iconOnly (forces a square: size-8/size-6 at small/xs); leadingIcon / trailingIcon take a component reference (RiAddLine, not <RiAddLine/>); type defaults to 'button'; ref is a plain prop (React 19). ButtonLink has the same props on <a>. The style map is exported as `buttonStyles`. Hover gradient: CSS cannot transition background-image, so @utility bg-button-primary fades a ::before layer holding the hover gradient. @utility button-press-motion scales to 0.98 on :active with an asymmetric return (420ms) and turns off under reduced motion. Disabled handling covers both :disabled and [aria-disabled=true]. directionalIconClass() mirrors arrow icons in RTL. There is no loading, asChild/render prop or fullWidth.

standout.name: AlertDialog + Modal compound (registry: components/base/modal/modal.tsx)
standout.why: The confirm-delete flow every admin panel needs, solved properly: an async confirm keeps the dialog open, a spinner sits in the button's icon slot, and Cancel and Escape are locked while pending.
standout.apiNotes: Parts: ModalTrigger (first child is the trigger, wrapped in RAC Pressable), Modal, ModalHeader, ModalBody, ModalFooter. Modal takes size 'sm'|'md'|'lg'|'xl' (400 to 800px), role, overlayClassName, isDismissable, children as a node or a ({close}) => node render prop. A useModalClose() hook is exported. AlertDialog takes title, description, variant 'danger'|'default', icon|false, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, onConfirm: () => void|Promise (a returned promise keeps the dialog open, sets aria-busy and shows a PendingGlyph spinner as leadingIcon; it closes on resolve and stays open on reject), pendingLabel, isConfirmDisabled (for example until a confirmation phrase is typed), and isDismissable (default false). Motion: the panel goes from scale 0.85 plus 4px blur on cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1) behind motion-safe:, so reduced motion keeps only the fade. Registry-only today, not on GitHub yet.

standout.name: Toast / Toaster (registry: components/base/toast/toast.tsx)
standout.why: A Sonner-style imperative API in about 250 lines with no dependency, reusing the Notification card. A good model for a toast system the user owns.
standout.apiNotes: toast(title, opts) returns an id. Helpers: toast.success / error / info; toast.update(id, {title, status, duration}) restarts the countdown; toast.dismiss(id?). Options: id (reusing an id replaces the toast), description, status, icon, avatar, actions[] (pressing one also dismisses), duration (Infinity keeps it open), dismissible, onDismiss. Toaster takes position (default 'bottom-end'), limit (3), duration (5000), aria-label and closeLabel. The store is a module-level array read with useSyncExternalStore. Only the first mounted Toaster renders (owner election), so nested layouts never show a toast twice. Countdowns pause on hover or focus. The region is aria-live polite. Registry-only today.

standout.name: SegmentedControl (components/base/segmented-control/segmented-control.tsx)
standout.why: The Weekly/Monthly/Yearly switch every dashboard has. The thumb is measured rather than computed, so it works with any label width, in RTL and when the label is translated.
standout.apiNotes: Built on RAC ToggleButtonGroup with selectionMode='single' and disallowEmptySelection set internally. Props: everything ToggleButtonGroup takes (selectedKeys, defaultSelectedKeys, onSelectionChange, aria-label) plus variant 'solid'|'plain'. Children are SegmentedControlItem elements with an id. A ResizeObserver plus a MutationObserver watch [data-selected] and move an absolutely positioned thumb with a transform transition. It re-measures when the direction changes. className accepts RAC's (state) => string function form.

standout.name: Switch / SwitchTrack / SwitchCard (components/base/switch/switch.tsx)
standout.why: Splits presentation from behaviour: one SwitchTrack visual is reused by Switch, SwitchCard and ThemeToggle. Size and shape form a small matrix with RTL-aware travel.
standout.apiNotes: Switch takes the RAC Switch props plus size 'sm'(28×16)|'md'(42×24)|'lg'(56×32) and shape 'pill'|'rectangle'. SwitchTrack({state:{isSelected,isDisabled,isFocusVisible}, size, shape}) is pure visuals. Per-size settings live in an exported `switchSizes` map (track, thumb, travel 'translate-x-3 rtl:-translate-x-3', and so on). The 'on' state uses an accent-500 to accent-600 gradient, so a re-tinted accent ramp flows through.

standout.name: ThemeToggle (components/application/theme/theme-toggle.tsx)
standout.why: A well-made light/dark control: a View Transitions circular reveal from the click point, a blurred-edge SVG mask, a keyboard fallback that starts from the element's centre, sync across tabs, and an instant change under reduced motion or in unsupported browsers.
standout.apiNotes: Props: appearance 'sidebar'|'segmented'|'sidebar-segmented'|'glass-segmented', size 'small'|'medium', collapsed, transitionDuration (820ms default), className. Also exported: applyTheme(theme, {persist}), applyThemeWithTransition(theme, {origin, element, duration}), useThemeMode() (useSyncExternalStore over the class on <html>), THEME_STORAGE_KEY 'boardui:theme'. Transitions are frozen during capture with a `.theme-transitioning *{transition:none!important}` class. Caveat: it never reads the OS preference and defaults to light.

standout.name: StatCards + useCountUp (components/application/dashboard/stat-cards.tsx, hooks/use-count-up.ts)
standout.why: The KPI row admin dashboards need, data-driven with two looks. The count-up hook is a ready-made counter animation.
standout.apiNotes: StatCards takes variant 'plain'|'footer', stats: Stat[] where Stat is {icon, label, value: string, delta: string, deltaColor 'lime'|'rose'|'neutral', tone?, caption?, hint? (shown in an info tooltip that opens on hover, focus and tap)}, plus count and columns 1|2|4, with a responsive grid built in. useCountUp(target, duration=320) eases from the previous value with easeOutCubic on requestAnimationFrame and has no reduced-motion check. Values are preformatted strings, so formatting stays with the caller's Intl. The footer tones use raw Tailwind palette gradients (from-blue-500), which breaks the system's own token rule.

standout.name: DatePicker / DateRangePicker / MeetingScheduler (components/base/date-picker/*)
standout.why: The calendar pattern to borrow: a draft-and-commit flow (Apply/Cancel), quick-select presets, editable date chips, and anchoring to an external trigger.
standout.apiNotes: value / defaultValue / onChange use @internationalized/date CalendarDate (or a range). onChange fires only on Apply, and Cancel restores the committed value. Also isDisabled, aria-label, and triggerRef + isOpen + onOpenChange to anchor the popover to your own element (BoardUI's trigger then hides). The Calendar is keyed on each open so its visible month re-syncs. The range picker shows two months with presets (Today, Yesterday, Last week, This month, Last month, This year, Last year, All time) computed on open. The summary chip animates with motion's AnimatePresence. UI strings ('Select date', 'Cancel', 'Apply') are hard-coded English.

standout.name: NumberField (registry: components/base/number-field/number-field.tsx)
standout.why: The correct base for a counter or stepper: locale-aware formatting and parsing, clamping, hold-to-repeat steppers, keyboard and wheel stepping, all from React Aria.
standout.apiNotes: Takes all RAC NumberField props (value, defaultValue, onChange, minValue, maxValue, step, formatOptions such as {style:'currency', currency:'USD'} or percent or unit, isWheelDisabled) plus label, hint, tooltip, placeholder, size 'medium'|'small', leadingIcon, hideSteppers, fieldClassName. Steppers are RAC Buttons with slot='decrement' / slot='increment', styled with data-[pressed], data-[focus-visible] and data-[disabled] attributes.

standout.name: DataGrid (components/application/data-grid/data-grid.tsx)
standout.why: A generic, typed spreadsheet grid for admin back-offices: editing, validation, summaries, CSV export and undo/redo with no AG Grid dependency.
standout.apiNotes: DataGrid<T> takes aria-label, data, columns: DataGridColumn<T>[] where each column is {key, header, width, type 'text'|'number'|'select', options, editable, filterable, min, max, align 'start'|'end', summary 'sum'|'average'|'count', format, formatSummary, validate(value,row) => error string}, plus getRowId, onDataChange (omit it for read-only), height, exportFileName, emptyState. Rows are virtualized at a fixed height. Contrast with DataTable, which exports only `DataTableExample` with hard-coded demo CUSTOMERS data: a recipe, not a reusable component.

standout.name: DirectionProvider + directionalIconClass (components/foundations/direction/direction.tsx, utils/directional-icon.ts)
standout.why: An RTL setup that also covers React Aria keyboard navigation and portalled overlays, which matters for the user's Arabic locale.
standout.apiNotes: DirectionProvider({locale}) wraps RAC I18nProvider and a display:contents <div lang dir>, and providers can be nested for mixed-language regions. useDirection() returns 'ltr'|'rtl'. directionalIconClass(icon) adds rtl:rotate-180 only for navigation arrows and sidebar glyphs, not logos, media controls or trend arrows. Tailwind variants: @custom-variant rtl (&:dir(rtl)), so the nearest direction boundary wins and not an ancestor selector.

standout.name: AgentThinking (components/application/agent-thinking/agent-thinking.tsx)
standout.why: A tasteful loading indicator with a shimmering label, useful beyond AI chat for any long-running admin job.
standout.apiNotes: Props: variant 'wave'|'spin'|'stars'|'infinity', label (default 'Thinking'), tone 'subtle'|'default'|'primary'|'accent', shimmer, showTimer (elapsed seconds), className. Uses role='status'. The dot grids run on a JS interval with a static first frame shared by SSR and reduced motion. Stars and infinity are CSS keyframes, and the shimmer is a background-clip:text gradient with a reduced-motion fallback.

buttonApi: Button and ButtonLink (separate components for <button> and <a>, sharing one style map) take variant 'primary'|'secondary'|'ghost'|'danger' and size 'medium' (h-9, 20px icon) | 'small' (h-8, 18px icon) | 'xs' (h-6, 14px icon). iconOnly forces a square. leadingIcon and trailingIcon take an icon component reference that the button sizes itself and mirrors in RTL. type defaults to "button", and ref is a plain React 19 prop. Disabled uses native `disabled` or aria-disabled. Siblings: IconButton / IconLinkButton (icon and an aria-label are required; sizes medium 36 and small 32; secondary look only); LinkButton (variant primary|secondary, sizes medium|small|xs, renders <a> when href is set and <button> otherwise, so it is polymorphic by href); ButtonGroup with ButtonGroupItem (role=group, sizes medium|small, `selected` sets aria-pressed, hairline dividers, iconOnly); CloseButton; SocialButton (24 providers, three colour treatments, icon-only form); SegmentedControl for exclusive selection. Missing: a loading/isPending prop (AlertDialog fakes one by passing a spinner as leadingIcon with aria-busy), asChild/render-prop polymorphism, fullWidth, and outline/tonal/elevated variants (no M3 filled-tonal or outlined equivalents beyond 'secondary'). Styling comes from plain objects (`sortCx`) merged with tailwind-merge, not CVA, and the map is exported as `buttonStyles`.
apiPatterns: Icon props take component references (leadingIcon={RiAddLine}) and the component applies the size class, so icon sizing cannot drift between call sites.
React 19 ref passed as a regular prop everywhere; no forwardRef.

Style maps are plain nested objects passed through an identity `sortCx()` (so Tailwind IntelliSense sorts them), merged with `cx` = extendTailwindMerge, and exported (`buttonStyles`, `linkButtonStyles`, `switchSizes`) for composition and a dev 'Design Tuner'.

tailwind-merge is extended with the custom composite text utilities (text-body-medium and the like) so it does not mistake them for colour classes and silently drop them. Critical if you build M3 type-scale utilities.

Token layering in Tailwind v4: @theme primitives, :root semantic tokens, .dark overrides, then @theme inline re-export. An 11-step accent-* ramp feeds every CTA and selection surface, so the brand re-tints by overriding 11 variables (and a [data-accent] hook).

Interactive gradient states as @utility classes: the default gradient is the background, and the hover gradient sits on a ::before that crossfades its opacity, because background-image cannot transition.
Press feedback as a reusable @utility button-press-motion: transform scale(0.98) with a short press and slower release, off for disabled and under prefers-reduced-motion.
React Aria render-prop className ((state) => cx(...)) and data-[pressed] / data-[focus-visible] / data-[disabled] / data-[entering] / data-[exiting] attributes for state styling.
Presentation split from behaviour: SwitchTrack and CheckboxGlyph are pure visuals shared by Switch, SwitchCard, CheckboxCard and ThemeToggle.
Compound components with render-prop children (Modal children = ({close}) => …) plus a useModalClose() hook, so footers can close without threading props.
Async-aware confirm: onConfirm may return a promise. The dialog stays open, the confirm button gets aria-busy and a spinner, and Cancel and Escape are disabled until it settles.
Imperative module store plus useSyncExternalStore for toasts and theme, with an owner election so duplicate <Toaster/>s render nothing.
Draft-and-commit for pickers: internal pendingValue, onChange only on Apply, and the Calendar remounted via a key on each open to re-sync the visible month.
External anchoring: triggerRef + isOpen + onOpenChange lets a popover attach to any element of the caller's.

RTL: DirectionProvider (RAC I18nProvider plus a display:contents dir/lang boundary), @custom-variant rtl (&:dir(rtl)), logical ps/pe/start/end everywhere, rtl:-translate-x on thumbs, and directionalIconClass for arrows only.
Reduced motion handled per animation (a @media block next to each keyframe, motion-safe: variants, matchMedia checks in JS), with deliberate choices such as the spinner slowing rather than stopping.
Theme switch through the View Transitions API with a click-origin mask, freezing component transitions during capture.

Accessibility details: role=status on loaders, polite live region for toasts, required aria-label typed into IconButton's props, focus-visible ring token (ring-border-focus-ring), 16px minimum input font on phones to stop iOS zoom.

Agent-native distribution: AGENTS.md / .cursor rules (semantic tokens only, composite type only, cx only, logical properties), an MCP server (list/search/get_component/get_usage_examples/get_theme), llms.txt, markdown docs via Accept: text/markdown, and a shadcn-schema registry with usage examples in item meta.
borrow: Distribution model: publish your own library as a shadcn-schema registry (/r/registry.json plus /r/{name}.json with registryDependencies and meta.example/snippets), so every project, and Claude Code, installs the same source with `npx shadcn add <url>`. No npm package or versioning hell, and it works for both static-export marketing sites and admin panels.

Ship an AGENTS.md / Claude skill and an llms.txt with the library, as BoardUI does, stating the rules (role tokens only, composite type utilities only, `cx` only, logical properties), so agents building future pages stay on-system.

Token architecture: keep your M3 role names but copy BoardUI's four-layer Tailwind v4 layout (@theme primitives, :root roles, .dark roles, @theme inline). Map their accent-50…950 idea onto the M3 primary tonal palette so a project re-brands by overriding one ramp.
Build M3 type-scale composite utilities (text-display-large, text-body-medium, and so on) as @utility and extend tailwind-merge with them exactly as utils/cx.ts does.

Button: copy the icon-as-component-reference API, iconOnly, the ButtonLink twin, button-press-motion and the ::before gradient crossfade. Add what is missing: an isPending/loading prop (borrow AlertDialog's aria-busy plus spinner-in-icon-slot), M3 variants (filled, tonal, outlined, text, elevated, danger), a fullWidth option, and Link from next-intl through a render prop or asChild.
Take AlertDialog's async onConfirm contract wholesale for admin delete and destructive flows.
Take the toast() / toast.update / toast.dismiss API and the single-owner Toaster for every app.
Take DataGridColumn<T> (type, editable, validate, summary, format, filterable) as the schema for an admin data grid, and treat DataTable only as a styling reference.
Use NumberField (RAC plus formatOptions plus steppers) as the 'sayaç arttırma' counter primitive, and useCountUp for animated KPI numbers, adding a reduced-motion short-circuit.
Use StatCards' Stat type (icon, label, preformatted value, delta, deltaColor, caption, hint) for KPI rows in user and admin panels.
SegmentedControl's measured-thumb technique and SwitchTrack's presentation-only split.
ThemeToggle's View Transitions click-origin reveal, adapted to also honour the system theme.
DirectionProvider plus directionalIconClass plus the rtl variant for your Arabic locale. It already solves RAC keyboard navigation and portal direction.
Date picker draft/Apply flow, quick-select presets and the external triggerRef pattern for calendars.
avoid: Pro tier: never copy or closely reimplement Pro components or templates (all charts except Revenue and Orders, Calendar, Composer family, Task List, Web Search, Agent Progress/Limits, Questionnaire, Project Board, Agent Avatar/Creator, Multi-agent Chat) into an open-source library. The BoardUI License forbids redistributing the source or a recognisable derivative and building anything that competes with BoardUI.

Registry-only free items (Modal, Toast, Drawer, Popover, Combobox, Command Palette, Number Field, and others) are not yet in the MIT GitHub repo, and their registry JSON carries no license field. Their license is unverified until they appear on GitHub, so wait or ask hi@boardui.com before vendoring them into an OSS library.
Keep the MIT copyright notice (Mertcan Dundar Esmergul) with any copied file, for example a NOTICE or THIRD_PARTY file plus a header, if you publish your library.

Primitive mismatch: BoardUI is built on react-aria-components and your projects use Radix. Mixing both in one library doubles overlay, focus and portal machinery. Pick one; RAC's I18n and RTL story is stronger for 18 locales.
The CLI and MCP send PostHog telemetry (deps posthog-node, @posthog/mcp). Set BOARDUI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 or use the shadcn CLI with the /r/*.json URLs.
Heavy inline commentary in every file, which your CLAUDE.md forbids. Strip it on import.

Hard-coded English UI strings ('Select date', 'Cancel', 'Apply', 'Thinking', 'From last month', 'Loading') and a JSX-walking `useTemplateCopy` translator that clones elements at runtime. Replace them with explicit label props fed from next-intl.

Token-rule violations inside components despite AGENTS.md: StatCards uses raw from-blue-500, ThemeToggle uses bg-[#2e2e33] and literal black/white, AgentThinking uses var(--color-blue-500). These need re-tokenising to M3 roles.

Visual language is BoardUI's own (blue gradients, skeuomorphic switch thumb, Inter, Figma pixel values such as h-[34px]). It is not Material 3, so treat it as a source of behaviour and API, not visuals.
Icon lock-in to @remixicon/react: directionalIconClass compares against specific Remix component references.
Dark mode is class-only and ThemeToggle ignores prefers-color-scheme (defaults to light).
useCountUp has no reduced-motion guard. DataTable is a demo with baked-in data, not a reusable table.
Chart cards pull in recharts (heavy), and most charts are Pro anyway.
The repo is a generated export that takes no PRs. Bugs go to email, the site registry is ahead of GitHub, and the last GitHub push was 2026-10-02.
fit: A strong fit as a source of admin and user-panel primitives and blocks, and as the template for how to distribute your own library. It shares most of your stack: React 19, Tailwind v4 with @theme and semantic tokens, motion, first-class RTL including Arabic, and dark mode through tokens. It uses react-aria-components instead of Radix and plain style maps instead of CVA. Copy free-tier MIT files (Switch, SegmentedControl, Input/NumberField/OTP, DatePicker/DateRangePicker, Select, Tabs, Tooltip, DataGrid, StatCards, Notification, Pagination, Tree View, ThemeToggle, DirectionProvider) with attribution. Re-token them to your M3 role names, strip comments and route strings through next-intl. Treat Pro and registry-only items as inspiration only. It does not cover marketing or landing effects; pair it with an effects source for those.

Focus moves to the next row or to the heading after the exit animation, and an aria-live region announces each sign-out. The spinner appears only for requests slower than 150 ms. A container query (@max-[30rem]) moves the action under the heading in narrow columns. Source: /r/active-sessions.json.
