buttonApi:
There are four separate buttons and no unified API.

1. **Button** (ui/button.tsx, shadcn-derived): cva `buttonVariants` with variant default|destructive|outline|secondary|ghost|link and size default|sm|lg|icon|icon-sm|icon-lg. It has `asChild` through Radix Slot and data-slot="button". There is no loading, leftIcon or rightIcon prop; icons are plain children sized by `[&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4`, and `has-[>svg]` tightens the padding.
2. **RaisedButton** (ui/raised-button.tsx): the same cva shape, with size default|sm|lg|icon, a single default variant, asChild, and a `color?: string` prop. That prop computes contrast text, border, hover and shadow as inline CSS variables at runtime.
3. **DashboardButton** (inside dashboard-shell.tsx): variant primary|secondary|muted|ghost|danger and size sm|md|icon, with defaults secondary/sm. It defaults to type="button" and its colours are component-scoped CSS variables.
4. **Single-purpose CTAs:** DiscoverButton ({label, href?, onClick?, className}; renders <a> when href is set) and InteractiveHoverButton (children only, from Magic UI).

Also: **ButtonGroup** (orientation horizontal|vertical, ButtonGroupText with asChild, ButtonGroupSeparator) and an internal SessionButton in active-sessions with variant, isPending (aria-busy plus a delayed spinner), buttonRef and active:scale-[0.97].
apiPatterns: Every part carries data-slot, and state is exposed as data attributes for styling: data-state, data-status, data-active, data-current, data-hovering, data-variant. Parents style children through group-data-[hovering]/strip:opacity-35 and data-[active]:scale-y-[1.08], so there are no extra className props.

Controllable state through a local useControllableState(value, defaultValue, onChange) hook, with consistent triplets: sessions/defaultSessions/onSessionsChange, activeItemId/defaultActiveItemId/onActiveItemChange, tab/defaultTab/onTabChange, sidebarWidth/defaultSidebarWidth/onSidebarWidthChange.

Polymorphic routing by injection: `linkComponent?: ElementType` goes into React context, and items with href render through it, so Next Link or next-intl Link works without the library importing Next. Primitives use asChild through Radix Slot.

Promise-aware action props: onRevoke and onRevokeOthers may return a Promise. The component owns the pending, error and success UI, removes a row only after resolve, keeps it with an inline role=alert error on reject, and shows a spinner only after SLOW_REQUEST_MS = 150.

SSR-safe client values through useSyncExternalStore with a null server snapshot: a shared 'now' clock that ticks every 30 seconds and refreshes on visibilitychange, a 'today' value that rolls over at UTC midnight, and the detected locale. This avoids hydration mismatches in relative dates.

Container queries instead of viewport breakpoints: @container with @max-[30rem]: and @2xl/dashboard-shell, plus ResizeObserver-driven density (90→60→30 bars). Blocks work inside panels, previews and split views.

Theming hooks are component-scoped CSS custom properties (--obsidian-<component>-<role>) with a `.dark` override. Portaled layers carry a second class (`obsidian-dashboard-shell-layer`) so menus outside the root keep the palette.

Accessibility details worth copying: a headingLevel prop so a block fits the page outline; role=grid with aria-activedescendant for a focusable chart; an aria-live polite announcer; focus restored to the next row or the heading after AnimatePresence onExitComplete; a confirm dialog that focuses Cancel first; aria-current="page" on active nav; WAI-ARIA tabs; a focus trap in the drawer; and a keyboard-operable resize handle (arrows step 10px, Home/End jump to the limits).

Reduced motion in the newer blocks: useReducedMotion() swaps springs for jumps or fades, and CSS files carry @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks that remove ping and pulse animations. Older blocks (flip-text, hover-img, v-prism) do not handle it.

One shared moving highlight per list: a single absolutely positioned motion.span follows the hovered item using offsetLeft/offsetTop and springs. It appears in place when the pointer comes from outside and glides when it moves within the list. The active indicator uses layoutId. Touch input skips the highlight.

Localization of formats, not strings: Intl.DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat and NumberFormat take a `locale` prop, but UI words are hard-coded English. The custom blocks have no RTL handling; only the shadcn Calendar uses rtl: variants.

Agent-friendly distribution: shadcn-compatible /r/{name}.json manifests embed full file contents and dependencies, alongside registry.json, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a Markdown copy of every page (Accept: text/markdown), an OpenAPI spec and a local MCP resource server. Generated output is rebuilt from source (npm run registry:build and agent:build), never edited by hand.
borrow: **Distribution:** ship the library the way ObsidianUI does, as a shadcn registry (registry.json plus /r/{name}.json with embedded files) with llms.txt and a per-component Markdown page. Projects copy the source and own it, which suits Tailwind v4 projects and static exports, and AI agents can install from it. Add an npm package later only if needed.
**Controlled and uncontrolled props:** adopt the value/defaultValue/onValueChange triplet and a shared useControllableState hook as a library-wide rule, and name callbacks on<Thing>Change.

**Routing:** add `linkComponent` (or asChild) to every navigational block so admin shells and sidebars accept next-intl's Link. That keeps the CLAUDE.md rule 'import Link from @/i18n/navigation' without the library depending on next-intl.

**Async actions:** model destructive or async actions as Promise-returning props with built-in pending, error and success UI, plus a 150 ms delayed spinner and optimistic removal only after resolve. This fits Supabase RPC calls in their admin panels.

**Port three blocks into the library:** ActiveSessions for user panels (Supabase auth sessions), StatusBars for admin health pages, and the DashboardShell layout ideas (resizable sidebar, sliding pill, filter-menu toolbar, confirm dialog with tone). Rewrite their colours onto Material 3 roles (accent→primary, accent-foreground→on-primary, muted→surface-container-high, border→outline-variant, danger-solid→error, success and warning→custom roles in theme.css). Replace hard-coded English with a `labels` or `messages` prop, or next-intl keys, and fix RTL by using start/end logical properties and mirroring ArrowLeft/ArrowRight under dir=rtl.

**Counters:** use NumberAnimation's reel technique, or the MIT @number-flow/react it already depends on, for the requested counters and stat cards. Pass format from Intl.NumberFormat(locale) instead of the en-US default.

**Button naming:** keep the shadcn-shaped cva Button but name variants after Material 3 so it reads like the Compose DS: filled, tonal, outlined, text, elevated, plus destructive. Add `loading` with aria-busy and a delayed spinner, and leading/trailing icon slots. A RaisedButton-style 'elevated' look can be ButtonV2, but drive it from theme tokens, not runtime colour parsing.

**Marketing entrances:** take the CSS-only interaction style of DiscoverButton (BEM class plus CSS variables plus a prefers-reduced-motion block). It needs no JavaScript animation loop, which matches the static-export site's tw-animate-css approach.

**Accessibility checklist per component:** headingLevel prop, focus restoration after exit animations, aria-live announcements, keyboard support for custom charts (role=grid with aria-activedescendant), and Cancel-first focus in confirm dialogs.
**Test layout:** one Vitest and Testing Library file per component (tests/components/<name>.test.tsx), with registry and docs generation enforced by a check script.
avoid: **ClickSpark:** do not copy it. It is a port of React Bits' ClickSpark, React Bits has been MIT + Commons Clause since 2025-02-08 (no redistribution 'in a bundle, or as a ported version'), and which version ObsidianUI started from is unverified. Write your own if you want the effect.

**Missing upstream notices:** do not copy shadcn-derived ui/* files or InteractiveHoverButton with only ObsidianUI's notice. ObsidianUI's LICENSE names only 'ObsidianUI' and the docs never credit shadcn or Magic UI. Keep the original MIT notices (2023 shadcn; Magic UI), and better still, take those files from upstream directly.
**Demo media:** do not reuse the images, videos, avatars or the 937 KB Golden Gate SVG. Terms §5 says demo media is not licensed.

**GSAP:** treat hover-img, draggable-marquee and text-stream as inspiration only for an open-source library. They pull in GSAP, whose 'Standard no charge' license is not OSI-approved, and draggable-marquee and text-stream are untyped .jsx.

**Heavy or pre-1.0 dependencies:** three.js and postprocessing (v-prism, art-gallery) and @paper-design/shaders-react 0.0.x (liquid-metal). analytics-dashboard is one monolithic demo app with a 67 KB CSS file and the author's avatar and email baked in as defaults; use it as inspiration only.

**Hard-coded English and no RTL:** StatusBars, ActiveSessions and DashboardShell hard-code English UI strings and use physical left/right positioning and arrow keys. They will not pass `npm run i18n:check`-style parity or Arabic RTL without rework.

**FlipText:** it splits text with split(''), which breaks Arabic joining, Thai and emoji. It has no aria-label, and its registry manifest is missing the required keyframes, which live only in the site's globals.css.

**RaisedButton:** it parses colours by inserting DOM nodes, hard-codes dark:bg-zinc-500, and invites arbitrary hex values through `color`. That conflicts with the 'no hex outside theme.css, use role names' convention.

**Upstream stability:** treat ObsidianUI as a moving target and do not depend on its registry URLs. It has one maintainer, git history was reset on 2026-09-23, the code is largely generated with the Factory Droid agent, and hosting recently moved to Cloudflare. Copy and vendor what you take.

**Theme model mismatch:** ObsidianUI uses shadcn tokens with a `.dark` class, and each block carries its own hex or oklch palette in a separate CSS file. Porting means remapping every --obsidian-* variable to M3 role tokens.
fit:
Medium as a source of blocks and API patterns, and low as a source of primitives.

**Stack:** it matches the user's stack almost exactly: React 19, Tailwind v4, cva, Radix, motion, a cn() helper and shadcn-registry distribution. Code ports with little friction, and the registry-plus-llms.txt model is a good template for how to ship their own library.

**Primitives:** most of its 'library' is a re-hosted copy of shadcn/ui primitives, so for buttons, forms, calendar, tables and sidebar the user should go to shadcn upstream and reskin with Material 3 roles.

**Original value:** about six blocks.
- DashboardShell, for admin panels.
- ActiveSessions, for logged-in user panels.
- StatusBars, for admin health and uptime pages.
- The NumberAnimation counter.
- DiscoverButton, ParallaxSlider and SplitShowcase, for marketing pages.

These are well engineered for accessibility and reduced motion. All of them need a token remap to M3 roles, i18n of hard-coded English strings for 18 locales, and RTL fixes before they meet the user's conventions.

**Role:** inspiration plus selective block source, copied with attribution. It is not a dependency.

standout.why: The most reusable piece for admin and user panels. It has no date-library dependency, takes its locale from Intl.DateTimeFormat, uses a discriminated union for single vs range mode, and has full keyboard grid navigation. The month header and grid slide in the direction you navigate.
standout.apiNotes: CalendarProps = {mode?:'single', value?, defaultValue?, onChange?(Date|null)} | {mode:'range', value?:DateRange{from,to}, onChange?(range)}, plus defaultMonth, minDate, maxDate, isDateDisabled(date), weekStartsOn: 0|1, locale. CalendarOptions = the base props without className, re-used by DatePickerProps and DateRangePickerProps (which add placeholder, align 'start'|'end', side Side|'auto', disabled). The local useControllableState(value, default, onChange) gives controlled/uncontrolled behaviour. role=grid, aria-current='date', aria-label from a dateStyle:'full' formatter, roving focus through data-date. Keys: arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Shift+PageUp/Down for a year. Gaps: weekStartsOn cannot be 6 (Saturday, used in Arabic locales), ArrowLeft/Right and the chevrons are not mirrored for RTL, the popover aria-label 'Choose date' is hard-coded English, and colours are raw neutral-900/dark: classes.

standout.name: StatCard / StatGrid
standout.why: The best dashboard KPI tile in the set. Good or bad news is semantic (goodWhen), so the delta colour is right for churn, latency and cost. It has a scrubbable sparkline and honours reduced motion.
standout.apiNotes: {label, value, trend:number[], trendLabels?, previous? (delta computed from it) | delta? (percent given directly), goodWhen?:'up'|'down', period?='vs previous period', format?(n)=>string, color?, animated?, className}. useReducedMotion() turns the count-up off. role=group with tabIndex=0 plus arrow-key scrubbing, an svg with role=img and an aria-label, and an sr-only aria-live status. The sparkline is hand-written SVG (monotonePath) and measures itself with useElementWidth. Gaps: defaultFormat is Intl 'en-US', the aria text ('up', 'down', 'trend from') is English, and CHART_COLORS are hex values.

standout.name: AdvancedDataTable (DataTable compound)
standout.why: A compound-component data table: a context provider with toolbar, filters, content and pagination parts plus a hook. Columns carry a priority that decides what survives in the responsive card view, which is the pattern an admin panel needs.
standout.apiNotes: <DataTable data columns getRowId defaultPageSize defaultViewMode:'auto'|'table'|'cards' renderSubComponent isLoading error accentColor> with children <DataTableToolbar title searchPlaceholder onBulkDelete onBulkExport/>, <DataTableFilters/>, <DataTableContent emptyTitle emptyDescription/>, <DataTablePagination pageSizeOptions/>. useDataTable() exposes sort, filters, selection (isIndeterminate), expansion, column visibility and pagination. ColumnDef<T> = {id, header, accessorKey|accessorFn, cell({row,value}), sortable, filterable, filterOptions, width, align, priority:'high'|'medium'|'low'}. Limits: client-side only (no manual/server pagination or sorting mode), lots of `any`, not built on TanStack Table.

standout.name: Sheet (sheet.tsx)
standout.why: A Radix-style compound API with velocity-based drag-to-dismiss. Each side has its own elastic and dismiss thresholds, which works well for mobile filter drawers.
standout.apiNotes: <Sheet open? defaultOpen? onOpenChange?> containing <SheetTrigger/>, <SheetContent side:'right'|'left'|'top'|'bottom' showClose?> and <SheetHeader/Title/Description/Body/Footer/Close>. A per-side config table sets {from, to, axis, elastic, dismiss:(PanInfo)=>offset>96 || velocity>500}. Hand-rolled: createPortal, role=dialog, aria-modal, title and description ids through useId, focus moved in and returned, a Tab trap, Escape and scroll lock. Uses dvh-capped heights.

standout.name: Sidebar
standout.why: An admin-shell sidebar that collapses to icons on desktop, becomes a drawer on mobile, and toggles with ⌘B or Ctrl+B. The data-driven sections keep app code small.
standout.apiNotes: {sections: {title?, items: {id, label, icon?, badge?, children?: {id, label, badge?}[]}[]}[], activeId, onActiveChange, header?, footer?, collapsed?/defaultCollapsed?/onCollapsedChange?, mobileOpen?/onMobileOpenChange?}. useSidebar() returns {collapsed} so header and footer can adapt, and SidebarTrigger is provided. The 768px breakpoint is checked with matchMedia in JS. It is data-driven rather than compound, which limits custom item rendering.

standout.name: SplitButton
standout.why: A primary action plus a dropdown of secondary actions, which comes up constantly in admin UIs (Save / Save as draft). It has a proper menu keyboard model.
standout.apiNotes: {label, onClick, options: {value, label, icon?, disabled?, onSelect?}[], size:'sm'|'md'|'lg', variant:'primary'|'secondary'|'danger'|'info', disabled}. The chevron has aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded. The menu uses role=menu and role=menuitem, ArrowUp/Down, and closes on Escape or Tab, and useReducedMotion is respected. Gap: aria-label 'More ${label} options' is hard-coded English.

standout.name: DragToConfirm
standout.why: A slide-to-confirm control for destructive actions (delete account, archive). It has keyboard support, which most such sliders do not, and optional haptics.
standout.apiNotes: {label, confirmedLabel, actionType:'delete'|'archive'|'confirm'|'submit'|'unlock'|'continue', variant:'default'|'danger'|'warning'|'info'|'success', size, icon, confirmedIcon, isConfirmed (controlled), onConfirm, onReset, autoResetDelay (0 disables), disabled, haptic (navigator.vibrate(22))}. role=slider with aria-valuenow. Enter, Space or ArrowRight confirms. useReducedMotion is respected. Not RTL-aware (ArrowRight and drag along +x only).

standout.name: AnimatedNumber (Animated Number Morph)
standout.why: An odometer-style counter where each digit is a spring-driven column of 0-9. This is the 'sayaç' (counter) the user asked about.
standout.apiNotes: {value, decimals?, prefix?, suffix?, stiffness?, damping?, mass?, useGrouping?, compact?, className}. A useSpring per digit drives a translateY of -n*10%. Weak spots worth fixing in a port: compact uses Intl 'en-US' and grouping is a regex inserting ',' (wrong for tr and de), text-[#FAFAFA] is hard-coded, there is no reduced-motion fallback, and aria-label sits on a plain span. Prefer Intl.NumberFormat(locale).formatToParts() with one column per numeric part, as NumberFlow does.

standout.name: Combobox
standout.why: A searchable select whose matching includes per-option keywords, for picking countries, users or projects in forms.
standout.apiNotes: {options: {value, label, description?, icon?, keywords?[], disabled?}[], value?/defaultValue?/onValueChange?(string|null), placeholder, searchPlaceholder, emptyText, align, disabled, aria-label}. role=combobox, listbox and option. ArrowUp/Down and Enter. Filtering is a substring match over label, description and keywords.

standout.name: OTP Input
standout.why: A one-time-code field with pop animation, paste-to-fill and SMS autofill.
standout.apiNotes: {length?, value?, onChange?, onComplete?, autoFocus?, disabled?, className?, boxClassName?, aria-label?}. inputMode='numeric', autoComplete='one-time-code' on the first box, paste strips non-digits and fills, Backspace moves back, role=group. Digits only, so alphanumeric codes are not supported.

standout.name: UndoToast
standout.why: Optimistic delete with an undo window and a progress bar, a good pattern for list and admin actions.
standout.apiNotes: {open, title, description, undoLabel, restoredMessage, duration, variant:'default'|'success'|'warning'|'error'|'info', position (6 corners/centers), onUndo, onDismiss, showProgress, icon}. role=status. It is a single controlled instance, not a toast queue or manager.

standout.name: motion-tokens.ts
standout.why: A small named library of spring presets with the reasoning written down. It is the cleanest idea in the repo to copy into a motion layer.
standout.apiNotes: motionTransitions = {springGentle (170/26/0.9), springSmooth (200/28/0.85), springSnappy (380/30/0.5, used by Button whileTap), springMorph (220/32/1.0, for layoutId), springResponsive (320/24/0.7), springSoft (150/22/0.9), easeSoft (0.32s, [0.22,1,0.36,1]), easeFast (0.2s, [0.2,0,0,1])}. The numbers are stiffness/damping/mass. Components import these instead of writing inline numbers. Calendar is an exception with its own inline spring (460/38/0.7).

buttonApi: src/components/ui/Button.tsx is forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement> over motion.button and extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'button'>,'children'>. Props: variant 'default'|'primary'|'secondary'|'outline'|'ghost'|'destructive'|'success'|'link'|'gradient' (default 'primary'; 'default' and 'primary' have identical classes); size 'sm'(h-8 px-3 text-xs rounded-md)|'md'(h-10)|'lg'(h-12 text-base)|'icon'(h-10 w-10), default 'md'; isLoading (Loader2 spinner replaces leftIcon, sets aria-busy and disabled); loadingText; leftIcon and rightIcon (ReactNode slots wrapped in shrink-0 spans); fullWidth; type defaults to 'button'. Tap feedback is whileTap {scale:0.97} with motionTransitions.springSnappy, off when disabled. Styling is two plain Record<variant,string> and Record<size,string> maps merged with cn(), not cva. Missing: asChild, a render prop or polymorphic `as`, so it cannot become a link; no colour axis separate from variant (destructive and success are baked-in rose and emerald); no ButtonGroup; no reduced-motion check in the file, although Button.meta.ts claims 'Respects prefers-reduced-motion'. Bugs to avoid when porting: the 'gradient' variant's shimmer uses group-hover:translate-x-full but the button never gets a `group` class, so the shimmer never runs. Disabled uses opacity-30 plus pointer-events-none, which is low contrast and also kills title tooltips. Colours rely on site-only CSS variables (--text-primary, --bg, --surface, --border) and a .focus-ring class that the registry item does not ship, so in a fresh project the button is unstyled. The site's docs table lists 8 variants and omits 'default'. Related button components: SplitButton, PressButton, MagneticButton (a `strength` prop), MorphingButton, LiquidRippleButton, RainbowButton (variant 'default'|'outline', size 'default'|'sm'|'lg'|'icon'), NeonEdgeButton, TypewriterButton, BookCallButton.
apiPatterns: Controlled and uncontrolled everywhere through one small useControllableState(value, defaultValue, onChange) hook (Calendar, DatePicker, Sheet, Sidebar), with the onChange held in a ref so callers can pass inline lambdas.
A discriminated union on `mode` for single vs range selection (CalendarSingleProps | CalendarRangeProps), so onChange gets the right type without overloads.
Shared option types (CalendarOptions = base props minus className) re-used by DatePicker and DateRangePicker, so the trigger component passes calendar options straight through.

Compound components plus a context hook for complex widgets: DataTable with Toolbar, Filters, Content, Pagination and useDataTable(); Sheet with Trigger, Content, Header, Title, Description, Body, Footer and Close; Stepper with StepPanels.
A data-driven config object per variant or side (Sheet SIDES table: from, to, axis, elastic, dismiss predicate), so behaviour is declarative and testable.

Semantic intent props instead of colours: StatCard goodWhen 'up'|'down', DragToConfirm actionType plus variant, Badge variant (soft, solid, outline) crossed with tone (neutral, success, warning, danger).
Named motion presets (motion-tokens.ts) imported by components instead of inline spring numbers.
MotionValue pipelines that never set React state per frame (pointer, MotionValue, spring, transform), documented in EvilEye and used in StatCard scrubbing.
useReducedMotion() gating in the better components (StatCard, SplitButton, DragToConfirm, AdvancedDataTable), with duration set to 0 rather than the animation removed.

Accessibility done by hand: APG grid keyboard model in Calendar, role=slider with aria-valuenow in DragToConfirm, menu or menuitem with roving focus in SplitButton, focus trap and focus return in Sheet, autoComplete='one-time-code' and paste fill in OTP, sr-only aria-live status in StatCard.

Per-component .meta.ts (title, category, props table, features, accessibility notes, usageCode, createdAt). A generator turns these into the shadcn registry.json, the website catalog, llms.txt, the sitemap and the ⌘K search from one source of truth (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
AST-based dependency detection in scripts/generate-registry.ts: imports are read to decide each registry item's npm dependencies and the shared lib files it needs.
borrow: The motion-token idea, mapped to the user's stack: a single motion.ts (or an M3 Expressive-style motion scheme mirroring the Compose app's spring specs) with named springs (gentle, snappy, morph, responsive) and easings. Every DS component imports from it, never inline numbers.

Calendar's dependency-free approach: Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale) for month, weekday and aria labels plus a mode union for single and range. Feed it the next-intl locale, widen weekStartsOn to 0-6 using Intl.Locale.prototype.getWeekInfo where available (Saturday-start for ar), and mirror arrow keys and chevrons when dir='rtl'.

StatCard's API (value, trend, previous|delta, goodWhen, period, format) as the KPI tile for admin and user dashboards, re-coloured to M3 roles (primary, tertiary, error) and given a locale-aware default format plus translated aria strings.

DataTable's compound shape and column `priority` for the responsive card fallback, but build it on @tanstack/react-table with a manual (server) mode for real admin data rather than copying the 1,000-line client-only implementation.
Sheet's per-side drag-to-dismiss thresholds (offset over 96px or velocity over 500) and elastic config, layered on Radix Dialog for focus management instead of a hand-rolled trap.
SplitButton, DragToConfirm (for delete-account style flows), UndoToast (as a variant inside a proper toast manager such as Sonner) and Combobox keywords matching as API references.

A rolling-digit counter (AnimatedNumber) rebuilt with Intl.NumberFormat(locale).formatToParts, tabular-nums, an aria-live wrapper and a reduced-motion jump, so it works for tr/de grouping and Arabic digits.

The repo's single-source-of-truth tooling: per-component meta (props, a11y notes, examples) generating the shadcn registry.json, docs pages and llms.txt. This suits an open-source library distributed as a shadcn registry next to an npm package.

A ButtonV2-style 'tactile' layer: keep the base Button as cva plus Radix Slot (asChild) and add motion feedback (whileTap scale 0.97 with the snappy spring) as an opt-in prop or a wrapper instead of a separate component family.

Keep the LICENSE notice. If any EasyUI file is copied or substantially adapted, add 'Portions adapted from EasyUI (c) 2026 Suraj Maurya, MIT' to a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES file, which satisfies MIT and fits the user's no-comments-in-code rule.
avoid: Do not install items as-is into an M3-themed project. Colours are raw Tailwind palette classes (neutral, emerald, rose, red, sky) and hex values, which breaks the 'role names only, no hex outside theme.css' convention. Button depends on --text-primary, --bg, --surface, --border and the .focus-ring class from EasyUI's own tokens.css and index.css, which the registry items do not ship (no cssVars or css in registry.json), so it renders unstyled.
`shadcn add` also writes EasyUI's lib/utils.ts (adds copyToClipboard and scrollToTop) and lib/motion-tokens.ts over your files, and it does not declare clsx or tailwind-merge as dependencies.

No headless primitives: dialogs, menus, popovers, combobox and tabs are hand-rolled. Quality varies. Sheet has a real focus trap, but MorphingDialog has no role=dialog and no focus trap, plus a fixed default layoutId 'morph-dialog', so two instances on a page collide. AnimatedTabs has no tablist, tab or tabpanel roles and no arrow-key navigation.
No RTL support (components.json rtl:false, no dir handling found): arrow keys, chevrons, slide directions and drag axes are LTR-only, which matters for the user's Arabic locale.

i18n gaps: hard-coded English aria strings ('Choose date', 'More … options', 'Close dialog', StatCard's 'up' and 'down') and 'en-US' or ','-regex number formatting in AnimatedNumber and chart-primitives.
Reduced-motion coverage is partial (about 30 files). Button's meta claims support its source does not implement, and AnimatedNumber, AnimatedTabs and MorphingDialog animate regardless.
Imports 'framer-motion' (the repo pins ^13). The user's stack uses 'motion', so switch imports to 'motion/react'. Mixing both packages ships two copies.

Many components are large single files (MoneyCard 43 KB, AdvancedDataTable 39 KB, AIResponse 37 KB, CarSmokePageTransition 37 KB) with demo-ish props such as DynamicIsland's avatar, name, role and socials, so they are closer to blocks than primitives. Canvas and particle effects (SparklesCore, ShootingStars, DotShader) carry runtime cost on static marketing pages.

Young, essentially single-author project (repo created 2026-08-17, 262 stars, 231 of about 241 commits by the owner) with no npm versioning or changelog. Pin to a commit if you pull from the registry.

Provenance caveat: the site says designs are 'inspired by designs … found across the internet' and offers removal on request. If a component visibly reproduces another library's signature design (names such as SparklesCore, Meteors and Rainbow Button also exist elsewhere), check the original's license before shipping it in an open-source library.
fit: Partial fit: good for inspiration and selective porting, not as a primitive source. The baseline matches the user's stack (React 19, Tailwind v4, 'use client' components that run in Next 15 App Router, framer-motion which is the 'motion' package, shadcn-registry distribution, MIT). The parts the user's library cares about most do not: there is no Radix (the user standardises on Radix and cva), no cva usage, no M3 role tokens (raw palette and hex instead), no RTL, English-only aria strings and en-US number formatting against 18 next-intl locales, and partial reduced-motion support. Best roles: (1) API and behaviour reference for dashboard and admin widgets: StatCard, Calendar/DateRangePicker, DataTable compound with priority-based card view, Sidebar with ⌘B, SplitButton, DragToConfirm, UndoToast, OTP; (2) a motion vocabulary through motion-tokens.ts and the tactile button and dock interactions for a 'V2' or effects tier; (3) a model for the library's tooling, where per-component meta.ts generates the shadcn registry.json, docs and llms.txt. Anything copied should be re-skinned to M3 roles, moved onto Radix primitives, made RTL- and locale-aware, and credited in a notices file (MIT allows this).
